# package iec61850

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850"
```

Package iec61850 is a pure-Go IEC 61850 stack: an MMS client and server (IEC 61850-8-1 over [github.com/otfabric/go-mms](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms)), GOOSE (IEC 61850-8-1) and Sampled Values (IEC 61850-9-2, UCA 9-2LE), with SCL (IEC 61850-6) parsing, validation and model binding. No cgo.

IEC 61850 concepts — logical devices, logical nodes, data objects, data attributes, functional constraints, object references, datasets, report, GOOSE and SV control blocks, quality, timestamps — are first-class Go types. Applications work with IEC 61850 semantics, not raw MMS domains, item IDs or alternate access selectors.

#### Packages {#hdr-Packages}

  - iec61850 (this package): MMS client ([Client](#type-client)) and server ([Server](#type-server)), including the server's GOOSE and SV engines and the client's GoCB and MSVCB access.
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/goose](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/goose): GOOSE frame codec, publisher and supervised subscriber, SCL binding.
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/sv](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/sv): Sampled Values frame codec, 9-2LE helpers, paced publisher and subscriber with loss accounting, SCL binding.
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/l2](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/l2): raw Ethernet transport (Linux AF\_PACKET, macOS/BSD BPF) and an in-memory hub, shared by goose and sv.
  - [github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/scl](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/scl) with scl/index and scl/validate: SCL parsing (schema editions 1.7 to 2007C5), normalized model, cross-reference index, semantic validation.

#### Quick start {#hdr-Quick_start}

	client, err := iec61850.Dial(ctx, "10.0.0.1:102", iec61850.DialOptions{
	    Retry: mms.DefaultRetryPolicy(),
	})
	if err != nil {
	    return err
	}
	defer func() { _ = client.Close(ctx) }()

	ref, _ := iec61850.ParseRef("LD1/MMXU1.PhV.phsA.cVal.mag.f[MX]")
	val, err := client.Read(ctx, ref)

The README and the examples directory have complete programs for the client, the server, GOOSE and SV.

#### Layering {#hdr-Layering}

  - go-tpkt / go-cotp: ISO transport over TCP
  - go-mms: generic MMS protocol (ISO 9506)
  - go-iec61850 (this module): IEC 61850 semantics over MMS, plus GOOSE and SV directly on Ethernet (package l2)

IEC 61850 semantics live here; the MMS wire protocol lives in go-mms.

#### Object references {#hdr-Object_references}

IEC 61850 object references follow the format:

	LD/LN.DO.DA[FC]

Use [ParseRef](#func-parseref) to parse references and [Ref.String](#func-ref-string) to format them. The [Ref](#type-ref) type provides helpers for parent/child navigation and MMS domain/item-ID translation.

#### Functional constraints {#hdr-Functional_constraints}

Functional constraints (FCs) classify data attributes by purpose: ST (status), MX (measured), SP (setpoint), CF (configuration), etc. Use [FunctionalConstraint.IsValid](#func-functionalconstraint-isvalid) or [ParseFC](#func-parsefc) to validate FC strings. Note that [ParseRef](#func-parseref) accepts unknown FC values by default; use [FunctionalConstraint.IsValid](#func-functionalconstraint-isvalid) for semantic validation after parsing.

#### IEC references vs MMS names {#hdr-IEC_references_vs_MMS_names}

This package uses IEC 61850 object references (LD/LN.DO.DA\[FC]) throughout its public API. The underlying MMS names use a different convention:

  - MMS domain = logical device name
  - MMS item ID = LN$FC$DO$DA (components joined by $)
  - MMS dataset/NVL name = LLN0$dsName

Use [Ref.ToMMS](#func-ref-tomms) for conversion when needed.

#### Errors {#hdr-Errors}

The package defines sentinel errors (ErrInvalidReference, ErrNotFound, ErrInvalidArgument, ErrProtocol, etc.) for use with [errors.Is](https://pkg.go.dev/errors#Is), and typed error structs ([ReferenceError](#type-referenceerror), [DecodeError](#type-decodeerror), [DataAccessError](#type-dataaccesserror), etc.) for use with [errors.As](https://pkg.go.dev/errors#As). Lower-level go-mms errors are wrapped with [fmt.Errorf](https://pkg.go.dev/fmt#Errorf) and %w to preserve the error chain.

#### Server {#hdr-Server}

The [Server](#type-server) type serves an IEC 61850 model built from SCL ([NewServerModelFromSCL](#func-newservermodelfromscl)) over MMS. It handles variable access, datasets, report control blocks with runtime report delivery, controls (direct, SBO, SBOw with CommandTermination), setting groups, journals, files, and the GOOSE and SV control blocks. Use [Server.EnableReports](#func-server-enablereports), [Server.EnableSettingGroups](#func-server-enablesettinggroups), [Server.EnableJournals](#func-server-enablejournals), [Server.EnableGOOSE](#func-server-enablegoose) and [Server.EnableSV](#func-server-enablesv) to start the runtime engines, and [Server.SetValue](#func-server-setvalue) to update process values: a change drives reports, journal entries, GOOSE state changes and SV samples. MMS client writes to RCB, SGCB, GoCB and MSVCB attributes are dispatched to the corresponding engine.

[ServerOptions](#type-serveroptions) provides first-class fields for common server configuration: [ServerIdentity](#type-serveridentity) for MMS Identify, FileProvider for MMS file services, Authenticate for association security, and OnConnect/OnDisconnect for connection lifecycle hooks. The MMS Status service is always registered and returns operational status. Use [Server.Capabilities](#func-server-capabilities) to query which services are active at runtime. Call [Server.Close](#func-server-close) for orderly shutdown of runtime engines.

#### Concurrency {#hdr-Concurrency}

[Client](#type-client) methods are safe for concurrent use. All server runtime engines (reports, controls, setting groups, journals, GOOSE, SV) are safe for concurrent use. Lock ordering follows engine-level lock → per-element lock. The control runtime uses per-registration mutexes for SBO state; the report engine uses engine-level RWMutex → per-RCB mutex. These have been validated with concurrent stress tests and Go's race detector.

Cross-LN dataset references are not supported. See [Server](#type-server) and [NewServerModelFromSCL](#func-newservermodelfromscl) for details and known limitations.

#### Logging {#hdr-Logging}

All logging uses [log/slog](https://pkg.go.dev/log/slog). Inject a logger via [DialOptions.Logger](#func-dialoptions-logger), [ClientOptions.Logger](#func-clientoptions-logger), or [ServerOptions.Logger](#func-serveroptions-logger). When nil, no logging is emitted. On Dial/NewServer, a nil nested MMS logger inherits the IEC logger; [iso.WithLogger](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms/transport/iso#WithLogger) is independent. [DialOptions.Metrics](#func-dialoptions-metrics), [ServerOptions.Metrics](#func-serveroptions-metrics) and the goose and sv Metrics interfaces expose counters. See OBSERVABILITY.md.

#### Stability {#hdr-Stability}

The module follows semantic versioning; the v1 API of every non-internal package, client and server alike, is stable. See COMPATIBILITY.md.

```go
var (
	// ErrWriteAccessDenied maps to object-access-denied: the client is not
	// allowed to change the object (access-violation, a read-only
	// component, an object that is not selected).
	ErrWriteAccessDenied = errors.New("iec61850: object access denied")

	// ErrWriteTemporarilyUnavailable maps to temporarily-unavailable: the
	// object is reserved by another client, or its writability depends on
	// the state of another object (instance-locked-by-other-client).
	ErrWriteTemporarilyUnavailable = errors.New("iec61850: temporarily unavailable")

	// ErrWriteTypeInconsistent maps to type-inconsistent: the value does
	// not match the type of the object (type-conflict).
	ErrWriteTypeInconsistent = errors.New("iec61850: type inconsistent")

	// ErrWriteValueInvalid maps to object-value-invalid: the value is of
	// the right type but out of range (parameter-value-inconsistent).
	ErrWriteValueInvalid = errors.New("iec61850: object value invalid")

	// ErrWriteHardwareFault maps to hardware-fault.
	ErrWriteHardwareFault = errors.New("iec61850: hardware fault")
)
```

Errors a server application callback ([SettingGroupHandler](#type-settinggrouphandler), [ControlHandler](#type-controlhandler)) can return, or wrap, to choose the MMS DataAccessError of the refused write (IEC 61850-8-1 8.1.3.4.4.2, Table 23). A callback may also return an [\*mms.DataAccessError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#DataAccessError) directly. An error that carries neither gets the default of the service (see each handler's documentation).

## Functions

### func ApplySCLAddress

```go
func ApplySCLAddress(opts *mms.DialOptions, ap scl.ConnectedAP) error
```

ApplySCLAddress sets the remote (called) ISO addressing of opts from the Address of an SCL ConnectedAP, the values an IED is configured with: OSI-TSEL, OSI-SSEL, OSI-PSEL, OSI-AP-Title and OSI-AE-Qualifier. A P-type the address does not carry leaves opts unchanged, so the go-mms default applies. The local (calling) addressing is not taken from SCL. Errors match ErrInvalidArgument and name the P-type.


BoolCtlVal creates a boolean control value.

```go
func BspCtlVal(bits []byte, bitLen int) *mms.Value
```

BspCtlVal creates a bitstring control value for BSC (binary step controllable) CDCs.

### func DPCCtlVal

```go
func DPCCtlVal(on bool) *mms.Value
```

DPCCtlVal creates the ctlVal of a double-point controllable (DPC): BOOLEAN, off (false) or on (true) (IEC 61850-7-3, DPC ctlVal).

### func DbposValue

```go
func DbposValue(on bool) *mms.Value
```

DbposValue creates a Dbpos value (IEC 61850-7-3 Dbpos, IEC 61850-8-1 8.1.2.1: a two-bit bitstring): 10 on (true), 01 off (false).

### func DpCtlVal

```go
func DpCtlVal(on bool) *mms.Value
```

DpCtlVal creates a Dbpos (double-point) value: a two-bit bitstring, 01=off, 10=on. That is the type of a DPC's stVal, not of its ctlVal.

Deprecated: the ctlVal of a DPC is BOOLEAN (IEC 61850-7-3, DPC); a server refuses this value in an Oper with type-inconsistent. Use [DPCCtlVal](#func-dpcctlval) (or [BoolCtlVal](#func-boolctlval)) for the ctlVal and [DbposValue](#func-dbposvalue) for a Dbpos status value.

EncodeQuality encodes an IEC 61850 quality as an MMS bit string value.

### func EncodeTimestamp

```go
func EncodeTimestamp(ts Timestamp) *mms.Value
```

EncodeTimestamp encodes an IEC 61850 timestamp as an MMS UTCTime value, including the TimeQuality byte.

The quality byte encodes leap-second awareness, clock failure, clock synchronization, and sub-second accuracy bits.

### func NewServerModelFromSCL

```go
func NewServerModelFromSCL(s *scl.SCL, iedName, apName string) (*servermodel.Model, error)
```

NewServerModelFromSCL builds a server data model from an SCL configuration. The iedName selects the IED; apName selects the AccessPoint (empty uses the first AccessPoint with a Server).

Each logical device is served as the MMS domain IEC 61850-8-1 names it, as the other IEC 61850 stacks do: LDevice@ldName when the SCL has one, otherwise the IED name followed by LDevice@inst ("InteropIEDInteropLD"). Data set members, report, GOOSE and SV control block references, and the keys of [Server.SetValue](#func-server-setvalue) use that name. Before v1.7.0 the domain was LDevice@inst alone; [NewServerModelFromSCLWithOptions](#func-newservermodelfromsclwithoptions) with [ServerModelOptions.InstanceDomainNames](#func-servermodeloptions-instancedomainnames) keeps that.

The expansion of the type templates stops at [scl.DefaultMaxExpandedNodes](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/scl#DefaultMaxExpandedNodes) data objects and attributes with an error that wraps ErrLimitExceeded and [scl.ErrLimitExceeded](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/scl#ErrLimitExceeded); [ServerModelOptions.MaxExpandedNodes](#func-servermodeloptions-maxexpandednodes) sets another limit. Type references nested deeper than [scl.DefaultMaxTypeDepth](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/scl#DefaultMaxTypeDepth) levels are refused with the same error.

This is a convenience wrapper around [servermodel.FromSCL](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/internal/servermodel#FromSCL).

### func NewServerModelFromSCLWithOptions

```go
func NewServerModelFromSCLWithOptions(s *scl.SCL, iedName, apName string, o ServerModelOptions) (*servermodel.Model, error)
```

NewServerModelFromSCLWithOptions is [NewServerModelFromSCL](#func-newservermodelfromscl) with options.

### func ParseAPTitle

```go
func ParseAPTitle(s string) (mms.APTitle, error)
```

ParseAPTitle parses an ACSE AP-title written as an object identifier with commas (the SCL OSI-AP-Title form, IEC 61850-8-1 Table 132: "1,3,9999,23"), dots or spaces between the arcs. An empty string returns a non-nil empty AP-title, which the dial options read as "omit". Errors match ErrInvalidArgument.

### func ParseSelector

```go
func ParseSelector(s string) ([]byte, error)
```

ParseSelector parses an OSI transport, session or presentation selector written in hex, as in SCL and on IED configuration screens: "0001", "00000001". An optional "0x" prefix is accepted. An empty string returns a non-nil empty selector, which the dial options read as "omit the parameter". Errors match ErrInvalidArgument.

### func StringCtlVal

```go
func StringCtlVal(v string) *mms.Value
```

StringCtlVal creates a visible-string control value.

## Types

### type AddCause

```go
type AddCause int
```

AddCause represents the AdditionalCause field in LastApplError, indicating why a control command was refused or failed. The values are the AddCause enumeration of IEC 61850-7-2 (control model, clause 20), as libiec61850 encodes them on the wire.

```go
const (
	AddCauseUnknown                     AddCause = 0
	AddCauseNotSupported                AddCause = 1
	AddCauseBlocked                     AddCause = 2 // blocked by switching hierarchy
	AddCauseSelectFailed                AddCause = 3
	AddCauseInvalidPosition             AddCause = 4
	AddCausePositionReached             AddCause = 5
	AddCauseParameterChange             AddCause = 6
	AddCauseStepLimit                   AddCause = 7
	AddCauseBlockedByMode               AddCause = 8
	AddCauseBlockedByProcess            AddCause = 9
	AddCauseBlockedByInterlocking       AddCause = 10
	AddCauseBlockedBySynchrocheck       AddCause = 11
	AddCauseCommandAlreadyExec          AddCause = 12
	AddCauseBlockedByHealth             AddCause = 13
	AddCause1ofN                        AddCause = 14
	AddCauseAbortionByCancel            AddCause = 15
	AddCauseTimeLimit                   AddCause = 16
	AddCauseAbortionByTrip              AddCause = 17
	AddCauseObjectNotSelected           AddCause = 18
	AddCauseObjectAlreadySelected       AddCause = 19
	AddCauseNoAccessAuthority           AddCause = 20
	AddCauseEndedWithOvershoot          AddCause = 21
	AddCauseAbortionDueToDeviation      AddCause = 22
	AddCauseAbortionByCommunicationLoss AddCause = 23
	AddCauseBlockedByCommand            AddCause = 24
	AddCauseNone                        AddCause = 25
	AddCauseInconsistentParameters      AddCause = 26
	AddCauseLockedByOtherClient         AddCause = 27
)
```

AddCause values (IEC 61850-7-2, clause 20).

#### func (AddCause) String

```go
func (c AddCause) String() string
```

String returns the additional cause name as IEC 61850-7-2 spells it.

### type BrowseNode

```go
type BrowseNode struct {
	// Name is the local component name (e.g., "stVal", "mag").
	Name string

	// Reference is the full IEC 61850 object reference.
	Reference Ref
}
```

BrowseNode represents a generic browse child returned by [Client.ListChildren](#func-client-listchildren). Unlike [DataObject](#type-dataobject), a BrowseNode does not imply that the node is a data object — it may be a sub-data object, data attribute, or any other child in the FC-merged browse view.

### type CacheStrategy

```go
type CacheStrategy int
```

CacheStrategy controls client-side caching of IEC 61850 model discovery results to reduce server load during repeated browse operations.

```go
const (
	// CacheNone disables caching. Every browse/discovery call hits
	// the server. This is the default.
	CacheNone CacheStrategy = iota

	// CacheExplicit enables a cache that is only populated via
	// explicit calls to [Client.RefreshCache] or
	// [Client.RefreshLDCache]. Browse methods consult the cache
	// if populated, otherwise fetch from the server without
	// storing the result. Use [Client.InvalidateCache] to clear.
	CacheExplicit

	// CacheLazy transparently caches results on first access.
	// Subsequent accesses reuse cached data. Explicit invalidation
	// and refresh are still available via [Client.InvalidateCache]
	// and [Client.RefreshCache].
	CacheLazy
)
```

### type CancelParams

```go
type CancelParams struct {
	// CtlVal is the control value from the original Operate that
	// is being cancelled. Required.
	CtlVal *mms.Value

	// Origin identifies the command originator. When nil, a default
	// Origin with OrCatRemoteControl and empty OrIdent is used.
	Origin *Origin

	// CtlNum is the control sequence number that matches the
	// original Operate or SelectWithValue. Zero, with CtlNumSet false,
	// means the ctlNum of the last SelectWithValue of the control.
	CtlNum uint8

	// CtlNumSet sends CtlNum as given, zero included.
	CtlNumSet bool

	// OperTm is the scheduled operation time from the original
	// Operate. A zero value means the original was immediate.
	OperTm time.Time

	// Test is the test status of the control sequence being cancelled
	// (IEC 61850-7-2 20.5.2.6: every command of a sequence carries the
	// same test status; IEC 61850-8-1 Table 88). Before v1.17.0 a
	// Cancel always sent FALSE.
	Test bool

	// TQuality, when set, is the TimeQuality of the T member; see
	// [OperateParams.TQuality].
	TQuality *TimeQuality
}
```

CancelParams contains parameters for an IEC 61850 Cancel command.

### type CheckConditions

```go
type CheckConditions uint8
```

CheckConditions represents the Check bitstring in a control command: BIT STRING { synchrocheck (0), interlock-check (1) } (IEC 61850-8-1), bit 0 being the most significant bit of the first octet, as libiec61850 reads it (MmsValue\_getBitStringBit). The constants are flags of this type, not wire positions.

```go
const (
	CheckSynchroCheck   CheckConditions = 1 << 0
	CheckInterlockCheck CheckConditions = 1 << 1
)
```

#### func (CheckConditions) Has

```go
func (c CheckConditions) Has(flag CheckConditions) bool
```

Has reports whether the given check bit is set.

### type Client

```go
type Client struct {

	// nil when CacheNone

	// true when created via Dial (we close the MMS client)

	// iedName is the IED name prefix used by the server to form MMS
	// domain names (from DialOptions.IEDName). When non-empty,
	// ldDomain prepends it and fetchLDs strips it.

	// watchStop ends the goroutine that closes the subscriptions when the
	// association ends; watchDone is closed when it has returned. Both
	// are set with the first subscription (initReportDispatch).

	// Control model reports (control_termination.go).

	// ctlNum of the last SelectWithValue per control
	// operTm in the Oper/SBOw/Cancel type
	// a Check member in the Cancel type
	// last LastApplError per addressed control

	// ctlAddressed are the controls (controlKey) this client sent a control
	// service to; only their LastApplError is kept in ctlLAE.

	// Test hooks for intercepting fetch calls (unexported, test-only).

}
```

Client is an IEC 61850 MMS client that wraps [mms.Client](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Client) with IEC 61850 semantics.

A Client is created via [Dial](#func-dial) (which establishes a new connection) or [NewClient](#func-newclient) (which wraps an existing [mms.Client](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Client)).

Close is idempotent: calling it multiple times is safe.

When the association ends (the server concludes or aborts it, or the connection is lost), [Client.Done](#func-client-done) is closed, [Client.Err](#func-client-err) says why, and the report subscriptions are closed: their Reports channels are closed. Requests then fail; a new association needs a new Client.

Concurrency: the Client is safe for concurrent use from multiple goroutines. It synchronizes its own state (cache, subscriptions, segmented report buffers, connection lifecycle) and delegates MMS wire-level concurrency to the underlying [mms.Client](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Client).

#### func Dial

```go
func Dial(ctx context.Context, addr string, opts DialOptions) (*Client, error)
```

Dial establishes a new IEC 61850 MMS connection to the specified address (host:port).

The context controls the connection timeout. The caller must call [Client.Close](#func-client-close) when done.

#### func NewClient

```go
func NewClient(mmsClient *mms.Client, opts ClientOptions) (*Client, error)
```

NewClient creates an IEC 61850 client wrapping an already-created [mms.Client](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Client). The caller retains ownership of the MMS client and is responsible for closing it separately.

Returns an error if mmsClient is nil.

Use this when you need custom MMS connection setup or want to share a single MMS client across layers.

The client installs its own InformationReport handler on the MMS client ([mms.Client.OnInformationReport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Client.OnInformationReport)) when it first subscribes to reports or sends a control (to receive LastApplError and CommandTermination), replacing a handler set before.

#### func (Client) Abort

```go
func (c *Client) Abort(ctx context.Context) error
```

Abort performs a hard, immediate abort of the connection without graceful shutdown. Use this for emergency teardown or protocol desync recovery.

If the client was created via [NewClient](#func-newclient), Abort only marks the IEC 61850 layer as closed without aborting the MMS client.

Abort closes the report subscriptions locally (their Reports channels are closed) and sends nothing: RCBs are not disabled and URCB reservations are not released. A server releases them when the association ends; with [NewClient](#func-newclient), where the association outlives the client, use [Client.Close](#func-client-close) or [ReportSubscription.Close](#func-reportsubscription-close) first.

Abort is idempotent.

#### func (Client) Cancel

```go
func (c *Client) Cancel(ctx context.Context, ref Ref, params CancelParams) error
```

Cancel sends a cancel command for a previously selected control.

The CancelParams should match the CtlVal, Origin, CtlNum and Test of the original Operate or SelectWithValue (IEC 61850-7-2 20.5.2: one control sequence). Without a ctlNum (CtlNum zero and CtlNumSet false) the ctlNum of the last SelectWithValue of the control on this client is used, as for [Client.Operate](#func-client-operate).

#### func (Client) CancelEditSG

```go
func (c *Client) CancelEditSG(ctx context.Context, ld string) error
```

CancelEditSG cancels the edit session this client holds: SelectEditSG with SettingGroupNumber 0 (IEC 61850-7-2 16.3.3.1).

#### func (Client) Close

```go
func (c *Client) Close(ctx context.Context) error
```

Close performs a graceful shutdown of the IEC 61850 client.

If the client was created via [Dial](#func-dial), Close also closes the underlying MMS connection. If created via [NewClient](#func-newclient), the caller is responsible for closing the MMS client.

The client transitions through open → closing → closed. During the closing phase new requests are refused with ErrClosed and subscription cleanup runs: every subscription is closed locally (its Reports channel is closed), then the RCBs the subscriptions enabled are disabled and the URCBs they reserved are released. The remote cleanup ends when ctx ends, and after 5 seconds at the latest. The Conclude of a client made by [Dial](#func-dial) ends the same way, after which the connection is closed, so Close returns also when the server does not answer. Remote cleanup errors during this phase are logged at Debug level because the connection may already be half-closed.

Close is idempotent.

#### func (Client) ConfirmEditSG

```go
func (c *Client) ConfirmEditSG(ctx context.Context, ld string) error
```

ConfirmEditSG confirms the current edit session by writing CnfEdit=true to the SGCB. The server copies the edited SE values into the edit group's storage and clears the edit session.

This must be called after [Client.SelectEditSG](#func-client-selecteditsg) and any [Client.SetEditSGValue](#func-client-seteditsgvalue) calls to commit the changes.

#### func (Client) CreateDataSet

```go
func (c *Client) CreateDataSet(ctx context.Context, ld, dsName string, members []DataSetMember) error
```

CreateDataSet creates a dynamic (deletable) data set on the server.

The ld parameter is the logical device (MMS domain) that owns the data set, dsName is the data set name as an MMS item ID (e.g. "LLN0$dsNew"), and members lists the FCDAs.

Each member must have a valid Ref with LN and FC, or explicit DomainID/ItemID. Members may reference data in different logical devices (cross-LD members); when a member's Ref.LD is empty, the owning ld is used as the default domain. The data set itself is always created under the specified ld.

Member field precedence: if DomainID and ItemID are set explicitly, they are used as-is. Otherwise they are derived from the member's Ref via [Ref.ToMMS](#func-ref-tomms), defaulting the domain to ld when Ref.LD is empty.

Dynamic data sets can be deleted with [Client.DeleteDataSet](#func-client-deletedataset).

A dsName beginning with "@" ("@dsNew") creates a non-persistent data set of this association (IEC 61850-7-2 13.2.2.2, 13.3.4): visible to this client only and deleted by the server when the association ends; ld then only defaults the members' LD. The same "@name" addresses it in [Client.GetDataSet](#func-client-getdataset), [Client.ReadDataSet](#func-client-readdataset), [Client.WriteDataSet](#func-client-writedataset) and [Client.DeleteDataSet](#func-client-deletedataset).

The name is checked before any request (IEC 61850-7-2 22.2): the part after "LN$" (or "@") has 1 to 32 characters, begins with a letter and uses A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and \_, the MMS item has at most 64 characters (IEC 61850-8-1 8.1.3.2.2); a member's FC must be a valid functional constraint other than XX (IEC 61850-8-1 7.3.1 NOTE 2). A violation returns ErrInvalidArgument.

#### func (Client) DeleteDataSet

```go
func (c *Client) DeleteDataSet(ctx context.Context, ld, dsName string) error
```

DeleteDataSet deletes a dynamic data set from the server.

Only dynamically created data sets (Deletable=true) can be deleted. Attempting to delete a static (SCL-configured) data set returns an error from the server.

#### func (Client) DeleteFile

```go
func (c *Client) DeleteFile(ctx context.Context, fileName string) error
```

DeleteFile deletes a file on the server.

#### func (Client) Done

```go
func (c *Client) Done() <-chan struct{}
```

Done returns a channel that is closed when the association of the client has ended: after [Client.Close](#func-client-close) or [Client.Abort](#func-client-abort) of a client made by [Dial](#func-dial), when the server concludes or aborts the association, or when the connection is lost. For a client made by [NewClient](#func-newclient) it is the association of the [mms.Client](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Client) it wraps ([mms.Client.Done](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Client.Done)), which Close and Abort of this Client do not end.

When the association ends, the report subscriptions are closed (their Reports channels are closed) as by Abort: nothing is sent.

#### func (Client) DownloadFile

```go
func (c *Client) DownloadFile(ctx context.Context, fileName string, w io.Writer) (*FileEntry, error)
```

DownloadFile streams a file from the server to the provided writer. This is the preferred method for large files as it does not buffer the entire file in memory.

The returned [FileEntry](#type-fileentry) contains the file metadata (size, timestamp). The actual number of bytes written may differ from FileEntry.Size if the server reports an approximate size: up to [FileLimits.SizeTolerance](#func-filelimits-sizetolerance) bytes more are accepted (DefaultFileSizeTolerance by default). A server that sends more, or more than [FileLimits.MaxEmptyChunks](#func-filelimits-maxemptychunks) consecutive answers without data, is stopped: the error wraps ErrLimitExceeded and the file is closed on the server. What was written to w until then stays written.

#### func (Client) Err

```go
func (c *Client) Err() error
```

Err returns nil while the association is up. After [Client.Done](#func-client-done) is closed it returns why the association ended; the error matches ErrClosed and [mms.ErrClosed](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#ErrClosed) ([errors.Is](https://pkg.go.dev/errors#Is)) and wraps the cause go-mms reports ([mms.Client.Err](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Client.Err)).

#### func (Client) FindPaths

```go
func (c *Client) FindPaths(ctx context.Context, query FindQuery) ([]Ref, error)
```

FindPaths searches the server model for references matching the query. This performs model discovery and then filters the results.

The Pattern field in [FindQuery](#type-findquery) supports glob matching via [path.Match](https://pkg.go.dev/path#Match). Matching is applied to the full object reference string (e.g., "LD/LN.DO.DA"):

  - '\*' matches any characters within a single path component (does not cross '/')
  - '?' matches a single character
  - '\[' brackets match character classes

For patterns that need to cross component boundaries, consider using MatchRegex mode instead.

Pattern matching is performed against the object reference without the \[FC] suffix. If the same object path exists under multiple FCs (e.g. ST and MX), it yields one result per FC because the full reference string (including FC) is used as the deduplication key. To get path-level deduplication, set FindQuery.FC to restrict results to a single functional constraint.

The FC field, when non-empty, filters to attributes with that FC. Results are deduplicated by full reference string (path + FC).

#### func (Client) GetActiveSGValue

```go
func (c *Client) GetActiveSGValue(ctx context.Context, ref Ref) (*Value, error)
```

GetActiveSGValue reads a data attribute value from the currently active setting group (FC=SG).

The ref must include LD, LN, and data path — the FC is forced to SG. This returns the active group's value regardless of any ongoing edit session.

#### func (Client) GetDataSet

```go
func (c *Client) GetDataSet(ctx context.Context, ld, dsName string) (*DataSet, error)
```

GetDataSet retrieves the definition (members) of a data set.

The ld parameter is the logical device (MMS domain) and dsName is the data set name as an MMS NVL item ID (e.g. "LLN0$dsName"). The returned [DataSet.Reference](#func-dataset-reference) uses IEC 61850 format (e.g. "LD/LLN0.dsName").

#### func (Client) GetEditSGValue

```go
func (c *Client) GetEditSGValue(ctx context.Context, ref Ref) (*Value, error)
```

GetEditSGValue reads a data attribute value from the current edit setting group (FC=SE). The ref must include LD, LN, and data path — the FC is forced to SE.

An edit session must be active (via [Client.SelectEditSG](#func-client-selecteditsg)) for the server to return edit-group values.

#### func (Client) GetFileAttributes

```go
func (c *Client) GetFileAttributes(ctx context.Context, fileName string) (*FileEntry, error)
```

GetFileAttributes retrieves the metadata (size, last modified) for a single file without reading its contents.

Implementation note: MMS does not define a dedicated metadata-only call. This method opens and immediately closes the file to obtain the metadata from the FileOpen response. If go-mms gains a pure metadata accessor (e.g., via FileDirectory with an exact path), this should switch to that to avoid the open/close overhead and potential server-side side effects.

#### func (Client) GetGoCB

```go
func (c *Client) GetGoCB(ctx context.Context, ld, gocbItemID string) (*GoCB, error)
```

GetGoCB reads a GOOSE control block. gocbItemID is the MMS item, e.g. "LLN0$GO$gcb01".

#### func (Client) GetMSVCB

```go
func (c *Client) GetMSVCB(ctx context.Context, ld, msvcbItemID string) (*MSVCB, error)
```

GetMSVCB reads a multicast SV control block. msvcbItemID is the MMS item, e.g. "LLN0$MS$MSVCB01".

#### func (Client) GetReportControlBlock

```go
func (c *Client) GetReportControlBlock(ctx context.Context, ld, rcbItemID string) (*ReportControlBlock, error)
```

GetReportControlBlock reads all attributes of a report control block from the server.

The ld parameter is the logical device (MMS domain) and rcbItemID is the RCB's MMS item ID (e.g. "LLN0$BR$brcb01" or "LLN0$RP$urcb01").

#### func (Client) GetSettingGroupInfo

```go
func (c *Client) GetSettingGroupInfo(ctx context.Context, ld string) (*SettingGroupInfo, error)
```

GetSettingGroupInfo reads the Setting Group Control Block (SGCB) from the given logical device and returns the current state.

The SGCB is located at LLN0$SP$SGCB in every LD that supports setting groups. Returns an error if the SGCB cannot be read or decoded.

#### func (Client) GetVariableType

```go
func (c *Client) GetVariableType(ctx context.Context, ref Ref) (*mms.TypeSpec, error)
```

GetVariableType retrieves the MMS type specification for a variable. The ref must be an object reference (LD/LN with path) and must include a functional constraint.

#### func (Client) InvalidateCache

```go
func (c *Client) InvalidateCache()
```

InvalidateCache clears all cached model data without re-fetching. Subsequent browse calls will fetch fresh data from the server. This is a no-op when caching is disabled (CacheNone).

#### func (Client) InvalidateLDCache

```go
func (c *Client) InvalidateLDCache(ld string)
```

InvalidateLDCache clears cached variable data and dataset definitions for a single logical device. This is a no-op when caching is disabled (CacheNone).

#### func (Client) ListChildren

```go
func (c *Client) ListChildren(ctx context.Context, ref Ref) ([]BrowseNode, error)
```

ListChildren returns the direct browse children (sub-data objects and data attributes) under the specified reference.

The ref must include at least LD and LN. When ref has a path (e.g., LD/LN.DO), this returns the direct children of that path. When ref has only LD/LN, this is equivalent to [Client.ListDataObjects](#func-client-listdataobjects) but returns [BrowseNode](#type-browsenode) instead of [DataObject](#type-dataobject).

Because MMS variable names are FC-qualified, the returned children are a merged view across all functional constraints. A child name like "stVal" may exist under both ST and MX; this method returns it once. Use [Client.TreeWithOptions](#func-client-treewithoptions) with IncludeFCs to discover which FCs apply, or specify an FC when reading/writing.

Results are sorted alphabetically by name.

#### func (Client) ListDataObjects

```go
func (c *Client) ListDataObjects(ctx context.Context, ld, ln string) ([]DataObject, error)
```

ListDataObjects returns the top-level data objects under the specified logical node.

The data objects are discovered by listing all named variables in the parent MMS domain, filtering for the specified LN, and extracting unique data object names (third $-delimited segment).

Results are sorted alphabetically by name.

#### func (Client) ListDataSets

```go
func (c *Client) ListDataSets(ctx context.Context, ld string) ([]string, error)
```

ListDataSets returns the names of all data sets (MMS Named Variable Lists) defined in the specified logical device (MMS domain).

The returned names are MMS item IDs (e.g., "LLN0$dsName").

Results are sorted alphabetically by name for deterministic output.

#### func (Client) ListFiles

```go
func (c *Client) ListFiles(ctx context.Context, pattern string) ([]FileEntry, error)
```

ListFiles returns the directory listing for the given file path pattern on the server. An empty pattern lists the root directory.

Pagination is handled internally; all matching entries are returned. Results are sorted by name for stable, deterministic output.

#### func (Client) ListJournals

```go
func (c *Client) ListJournals(ctx context.Context, ld string) ([]string, error)
```

ListJournals returns the names of all journals (logs) defined in the specified logical device (MMS domain).

#### func (Client) ListLogicalDevices

```go
func (c *Client) ListLogicalDevices(ctx context.Context) ([]LogicalDevice, error)
```

ListLogicalDevices returns the logical devices (MMS domains) available on the server.

Results are sorted alphabetically by name.

#### func (Client) ListLogicalNodes

```go
func (c *Client) ListLogicalNodes(ctx context.Context, ld string) ([]LogicalNode, error)
```

ListLogicalNodes returns the logical nodes within the specified logical device.

The logical nodes are discovered by listing all named variables in the MMS domain and extracting the unique first $-delimited segment (the LN name in IEC 61850 MMS mapping).

Results are sorted alphabetically by name.

#### func (Client) ListReports

```go
func (c *Client) ListReports(ctx context.Context, ld string) ([]string, error)
```

ListReports returns the names of all report control blocks in the specified logical device.

Discovery is by MMS item-name pattern: an item ID with exactly three '$'-separated segments where the second segment is "BR" or "RP" is treated as a RCB. This is a heuristic — it does not perform semantic verification (e.g., reading RCB attributes) to confirm the variable is actually a report control block.

When [StrictnessOptions.VerifyReportCandidates](#func-strictnessoptions-verifyreportcandidates) is true, each candidate is read from the server and decoded; items that fail to decode as a valid RCB structure are excluded. This is equivalent to calling [Client.ListReportsVerified](#func-client-listreportsverified).

The results include both buffered (BRCB, FC=BR) and unbuffered (URCB, FC=RP) report control blocks. Each returned name is an MMS item ID like "LLN0$BR$brcbName01" or "LLN0$RP$urcbName01".

Results are sorted alphabetically by name for deterministic output.

#### func (Client) ListReportsVerified

```go
func (c *Client) ListReportsVerified(ctx context.Context, ld string) ([]string, error)
```

ListReportsVerified returns verified report control block names by reading each heuristic candidate from the server and confirming it decodes as a valid RCB structure. This is slower than \[ListReports] (one MMS read per candidate) but eliminates false positives from naming collisions.

Candidates that fail to read or decode are silently excluded from the result and logged at Debug level.

#### func (Client) MMS

```go
func (c *Client) MMS() *mms.Client
```

MMS returns the underlying [mms.Client](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Client) for advanced operations that are not exposed by the IEC 61850 API.

#### Warning — unsafe escape hatch {#hdr-Warning___unsafe_escape_hatch}

The returned pointer is shared with this Client. Operations performed on it bypass all IEC 61850 state management and can silently corrupt higher-level invariants including:

  - Model cache freshness (raw MMS writes can change server state without invalidating the cached browse results).
  - Report subscription state (disabling or re-enabling an RCB directly may desynchronize the subscription table).
  - Connection lifecycle (calling Close or Abort on the returned client while the IEC 61850 layer owns it leads to double-close or use-after-close).

Rules:

  - Do NOT call Close or Abort on the returned client when the [Client](#type-client) was created via [Dial](#func-dial) (the IEC 61850 layer owns it).
  - After [Client.Close](#func-client-close) or [Client.Abort](#func-client-abort), the returned MMS client follows the underlying go-mms closed semantics (all calls return [mms.ErrClosed](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#ErrClosed)).
  - Treat this as a read-only escape hatch (e.g. Identify, Status, GetNameList) unless you fully understand the interaction with the IEC 61850 layer's state.

Most users should not need this method.

#### func (Client) ObtainFile

```go
func (c *Client) ObtainFile(ctx context.Context, sourceFile, destinationFile string) error
```

ObtainFile instructs the server to copy a file from sourceFile to destinationFile. This is the standard MMS file transfer mechanism for "uploading" data — the server fetches the source file.

In IEC 61850 deployments, ObtainFile is typically used for configuration file transfer (e.g. SCL/CID files) where the server pulls a file from an engineering workstation or another IED.

Note: MMS does not define a direct client-to-server file write (push) operation. ObtainFile is the closest equivalent, but it requires the server to be able to reach the source file path.

#### func (Client) Operate

```go
func (c *Client) Operate(ctx context.Context, ref Ref, params OperateParams) error
```

Operate performs a direct-operate control command on the specified data object.

The ref identifies the controllable data object (e.g. "LD/LN.SPCSO1"). It must include LD and LN with a data-object path but must NOT include FC — the library writes to CO/Oper automatically.

For SBO control models, use [Client.Select](#func-client-select) or [Client.SelectWithValue](#func-client-selectwithvalue) before calling Operate.

The ctlNum is params.CtlNum when it is not zero or params.CtlNumSet is true. Otherwise it is the ctlNum of the last [Client.SelectWithValue](#func-client-selectwithvalue) of this control on this client, so that Select and Operate of one control sequence carry the same ctlNum (IEC 61850-7-2 20.5.2.4), or, without one, the next value of an auto-incrementing counter. If params.Origin is nil, a default Origin with OrCatRemoteControl is used.

The Oper carries operTm when the server's Oper type has it (learned once per control with GetVariableAccessAttributes), all zero for an immediate operate (IEC 61850-8-1 20.10.2.2); a non-zero params.OperTm requests a TimeActivatedOperate.

#### func (Client) OperateWait

```go
func (c *Client) OperateWait(ctx context.Context, ref Ref, params OperateParams) (*CommandTermination, error)
```

OperateWait operates a control with enhanced security (CtlModelDirectEnhanced or CtlModelSBOEnhanced, after [Client.SelectWithValue](#func-client-selectwithvalue)) and waits for its CommandTermination.

A refused operate returns the [ControlError](#type-controlerror) of [Client.Operate](#func-client-operate), carrying the server's LastApplError when it sent one. A negative termination returns the termination and a [ControlError](#type-controlerror) wrapping ErrCommandTerminationNegative with the LastApplError's AddCause. The wait ends with ctx: servers send no CommandTermination for controls with normal security, so do not use OperateWait for them.

#### func (Client) Read

```go
func (c *Client) Read(ctx context.Context, ref Ref) (*Value, error)
```

Read reads a single IEC 61850 data attribute and returns it as an IEC 61850 [Value](#type-value).

The ref must include LD, LN, and FC.

LN-level reads are supported: when the ref has LD + LN + FC but no path, the server returns the full structured value for all data attributes under that LN and FC combination.

For raw MMS values without the IEC 61850 wrapper, use [Client.ReadRaw](#func-client-readraw).

#### func (Client) ReadComponent

```go
func (c *Client) ReadComponent(ctx context.Context, ref Ref, component string) (*Value, error)
```

ReadComponent reads a named component (sub-attribute) of a data object or data attribute.

This is a convenience API equivalent to reading with a ref that has the component appended to the path. For example, reading component "stVal" from ref "LD/LN.Mod\[ST]" is equivalent to reading "LD/LN.Mod.stVal\[ST]".

The ref must include LD, LN, FC, and at least one path component (the parent structure). The component name must be non-empty and must not contain separator characters.

#### func (Client) ReadCtlModel

```go
func (c *Client) ReadCtlModel(ctx context.Context, ref Ref) (CtlModel, error)
```

ReadCtlModel reads the ctlModel attribute of a controllable data object. This determines which control flow (direct, SBO, enhanced) should be used.

The ref identifies the data object (e.g. "LD/LN.SPCSO1") without FC — the library reads from CF/ctlModel automatically.

#### func (Client) ReadDataSet

```go
func (c *Client) ReadDataSet(ctx context.Context, ld, dsName string) ([]DataSetValue, error)
```

ReadDataSet reads all member values of a data set in a single MMS request.

The ld parameter is the logical device (MMS domain) and dsName is the data set name (MMS item ID, e.g. "LLN0$dsName").

To understand the structure of the returned values, first call [Client.GetDataSet](#func-client-getdataset) to obtain the member definitions.

#### func (Client) ReadFile

```go
func (c *Client) ReadFile(ctx context.Context, fileName string) ([]byte, *FileEntry, error)
```

ReadFile reads an entire file from the server and returns its contents.

The file is held in memory, so ReadFile reads at most [FileLimits.MaxSize](#func-filelimits-maxsize) bytes (DefaultMaxFileSize by default): a file whose announced size is larger is refused before it is read, and a server that sends more is stopped. A server that sends more than [FileLimits.SizeTolerance](#func-filelimits-sizetolerance) bytes beyond the size it announced, or more than [FileLimits.MaxEmptyChunks](#func-filelimits-maxemptychunks) consecutive answers without data, is stopped too. The error then wraps ErrLimitExceeded and the file is closed on the server.

For large files, prefer [Client.DownloadFile](#func-client-downloadfile) which streams to an [io.Writer](https://pkg.go.dev/io#Writer) without buffering the entire file in memory.

#### func (Client) ReadJournal

```go
func (c *Client) ReadJournal(ctx context.Context, ld, journal string, start, stop time.Time) (*JournalReadResult, error)
```

ReadJournal reads journal entries within the given time range \[start, stop] from the specified journal in the logical device.

RangeStartTime and RangeStopTime are optional in QueryLogByTime (IEC 61850-7-2 §17.3.5.2): a zero start reads from the first entry and a zero stop up to the last. The MMS ReadJournal request always carries both, so they are sent as the first and last instant a BinaryTime can hold (1984-01-01 and 2163-06-05 23:59:59.999 UTC).

The returned entries are in chronological order. When [JournalReadResult.MoreFollows](#func-journalreadresult-morefollows) is true, use [Client.ReadJournalAfter](#func-client-readjournalafter) with the last entry's OccurrenceTime and EntryID to page through remaining entries.

#### func (Client) ReadJournalAfter

```go
func (c *Client) ReadJournalAfter(ctx context.Context, ld, journal string, afterTime time.Time, afterID []byte) (*JournalReadResult, error)
```

ReadJournalAfter reads journal entries starting after the given cursor position. Use the last entry's OccurrenceTime and EntryID from a previous \[ReadJournal] or \[ReadJournalAfter] call to page through journal data.

#### func (Client) ReadJournalAfterAll

```go
func (c *Client) ReadJournalAfterAll(ctx context.Context, ld, journal string, afterTime time.Time, afterID []byte) ([]JournalEntry, error)
```

ReadJournalAfterAll reads all journal entries starting after the given cursor, automatically following pagination until all entries are retrieved.

This is the paginating equivalent of [Client.ReadJournalAfter](#func-client-readjournalafter), with the limits and the cursor check of [Client.ReadJournalAll](#func-client-readjournalall).

#### func (Client) ReadJournalAll

```go
func (c *Client) ReadJournalAll(ctx context.Context, ld, journal string, start, stop time.Time) ([]JournalEntry, error)
```

ReadJournalAll reads all journal entries within the given time range, automatically following pagination (MoreFollows) until all entries are retrieved.

Entries are returned in chronological order. The stop condition is MoreFollows=false from the server. Same-timestamp cursor semantics are handled correctly via EntryID-based continuation. A page whose last entry is a cursor already used (the pagination does not advance) is refused.

The entries collected are bounded by [ClientOptions.JournalLimits](#func-clientoptions-journallimits) (1,000,000 entries and an estimated 256 MiB by default): a journal beyond a limit is given up with an error that wraps ErrLimitExceeded. For very large journals, use the paginated [Client.ReadJournal](#func-client-readjournal) / [Client.ReadJournalAfter](#func-client-readjournalafter) pair.

#### func (Client) ReadLastApplError

```go
func (c *Client) ReadLastApplError(ctx context.Context, ref Ref) (*LastApplError, error)
```

ReadLastApplError returns the last LastApplError this client received for the control object ref (or, for a ref without a data object, for any control of that logical node). The client keeps the LastApplError of the controls it sent a control service to ([Client.Select](#func-client-select), [Client.SelectWithValue](#func-client-selectwithvalue), [Client.Operate](#func-client-operate), [Client.OperateWait](#func-client-operatewait), [Client.Cancel](#func-client-cancel)), one per control; a LastApplError that names another control is not kept.

LastApplError is a VMD-specific MMS variable a server creates, reports and deletes at once (IEC 61850-8-1 20.11); it cannot be read. When none was received, ReadLastApplError reads the vendor extension LD/LN$CO$LastApplError, which conforming servers do not have.

Deprecated: use [ControlError.LastApplError](#func-controlerror-lastapplerror) of the refused control call, or [CommandTermination.LastApplError](#func-commandtermination-lastapplerror); they carry the LastApplError of that command.

#### func (Client) ReadMultiple

```go
func (c *Client) ReadMultiple(ctx context.Context, refs []Ref) ([]ReadResult, error)
```

ReadMultiple reads multiple IEC 61850 data objects or data attributes in a single MMS request.

Each ref must be an object reference (LD, LN, FC, and at least one path component). LN-level bulk reads are not supported; use [Client.Read](#func-client-read) for those. Results are returned in the same order as the input refs.

Duplicate refs are preserved: if the same ref appears multiple times, each occurrence produces a separate result at the corresponding index. The server may return identical or different values depending on timing.

Per-item errors (e.g., object not found) are reported in [ReadResult.Err](#func-readresult-err) as a [\*DataAccessError](#type-dataaccesserror) rather than failing the entire operation.

Mixed-domain and mixed-FC reads are supported: refs may span different logical devices and functional constraints within a single call.

If the MMS request itself fails (e.g., connection error), a non-nil error is returned and the result slice is nil.

#### func (Client) ReadRaw

```go
func (c *Client) ReadRaw(ctx context.Context, ref Ref) (*mms.Value, error)
```

ReadRaw reads a single IEC 61850 data attribute and returns the underlying [mms.Value](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Value) directly, without IEC 61850 wrapping.

This is useful when callers need full control over MMS value interpretation or want to avoid the [Value](#type-value) abstraction overhead.

Both object-level (LD/LN.DO.DA\[FC]) and LN-level (LD/LN\[FC]) reads are supported. LN-level reads return the full structured value for the LN + FC combination as a single MMS structure.

#### func (Client) RefreshCache

```go
func (c *Client) RefreshCache(ctx context.Context) error
```

RefreshCache re-fetches all cached model data from the server. This is a no-op when caching is disabled (CacheNone).

Use this after server model changes to ensure the client sees the latest structure. The cache is rebuilt atomically: on failure, the previous cache state is preserved.

#### func (Client) RefreshLDCache

```go
func (c *Client) RefreshLDCache(ctx context.Context, ld string) error
```

RefreshLDCache re-fetches cached variable data for a single logical device. This is a no-op when caching is disabled (CacheNone).

Only the per-LD variable list is refreshed; the global logical device list is not modified. If the LD was added or removed on the server, call [Client.RefreshCache](#func-client-refreshcache) instead to refresh both.

Both the raw item list and any derived parsed-ref cache for the LD are replaced atomically. Dataset definitions are preserved — call [Client.InvalidateLDCache](#func-client-invalidateldcache) to clear those as well.

#### func (Client) ReleaseURCB

```go
func (c *Client) ReleaseURCB(ctx context.Context, ld, rcbItemID string) error
```

ReleaseURCB releases a previously reserved unbuffered report control block.

The caller should disable the report (RptEna=false) before releasing to avoid undefined behavior.

#### func (Client) RenameFile

```go
func (c *Client) RenameFile(ctx context.Context, currentName, newName string) error
```

RenameFile renames a file on the server.

#### func (Client) ReserveURCB

```go
func (c *Client) ReserveURCB(ctx context.Context, ld, rcbItemID string) error
```

ReserveURCB reserves an unbuffered report control block for exclusive use by this client.

Reservation is required before configuring or enabling a URCB. The reservation remains until explicitly released via [Client.ReleaseURCB](#func-client-releaseurcb) or the connection is closed.

#### func (Client) Select

```go
func (c *Client) Select(ctx context.Context, ref Ref) (string, error)
```

Select performs a select-before-operate (SBO) select command.

This is used with CtlModelSBONormal. The server returns the selected object reference on success. The client must then call [Client.Operate](#func-client-operate) within the server's select timeout.

For enhanced security SBO (CtlModelSBOEnhanced), use [Client.SelectWithValue](#func-client-selectwithvalue) instead.

#### Interoperability note {#hdr-Interoperability_note}

The SBO decode path assumes the server returns a VisibleString from a normal MMS read on the SBO subattribute. An empty string is interpreted as "select denied". This matches IEC 61850-8-1 § 22.2 for normal-security SBO but behaviour may vary across devices. Validate against your target devices before relying on this in production.

#### func (Client) SelectActiveSG

```go
func (c *Client) SelectActiveSG(ctx context.Context, ld string, sg uint8) error
```

SelectActiveSG writes a new active setting group number to the SGCB. The server activates the specified group, making its SE values available via FC=SG reads.

The sg parameter must be in \[1, NumOfSGs]. Use [Client.GetSettingGroupInfo](#func-client-getsettinggroupinfo) to discover the valid range.

#### func (Client) SelectEditSG

```go
func (c *Client) SelectEditSG(ctx context.Context, ld string, sg uint8) error
```

SelectEditSG selects a setting group for editing. This reserves the edit session; the server sets EditSG in the SGCB to the requested group number. Only one client may hold an edit session at a time.

After selecting, use [Client.GetEditSGValue](#func-client-geteditsgvalue) and [Client.SetEditSGValue](#func-client-seteditsgvalue) to read/write SE-constrained values for the edit group. Call [Client.ConfirmEditSG](#func-client-confirmeditsg) to commit changes.

The sg parameter is in \[1, NumOfSGs], or 0 to cancel the edit and release the reservation (IEC 61850-7-2 16.3.3.1); see [Client.CancelEditSG](#func-client-canceleditsg). Before v1.17.0, 0 was refused.

#### func (Client) SelectWithValue

```go
func (c *Client) SelectWithValue(ctx context.Context, ref Ref, params OperateParams) error
```

SelectWithValue performs a select-before-operate with enhanced security (SBOw) by writing the full Oper structure to the SBOw subattribute.

This is used with CtlModelSBOEnhanced. On success the select is held by the server; the client must then call [Client.Operate](#func-client-operate) with the same parameters within the server's select timeout.

The ctlNum is params.CtlNum when it is not zero or params.CtlNumSet is true, else the next value of an auto-incrementing counter. It is remembered for the control: an Operate or Cancel of it on this client without a ctlNum of its own reuses it (IEC 61850-7-2 20.5.2.4: one control sequence, one ctlNum).

#### func (Client) SetEditSGValue

```go
func (c *Client) SetEditSGValue(ctx context.Context, ref Ref, value *mms.Value) error
```

SetEditSGValue writes a data attribute value into the current edit setting group (FC=SE). The ref must include LD, LN, and data path — the FC is forced to SE.

An edit session must be active (via [Client.SelectEditSG](#func-client-selecteditsg)). The change is not committed until [Client.ConfirmEditSG](#func-client-confirmeditsg) is called.

#### func (Client) SetGoCB

```go
func (c *Client) SetGoCB(ctx context.Context, ld, gocbItemID string, upd GoCBUpdate) error
```

SetGoCB writes the selected GoCB attributes, GoEna last.

#### func (Client) SetMSVCB

```go
func (c *Client) SetMSVCB(ctx context.Context, ld, msvcbItemID string, upd MSVCBUpdate) error
```

SetMSVCB writes the selected MSVCB attributes, SvEna last.

#### func (Client) SetReportControlBlock

```go
func (c *Client) SetReportControlBlock(ctx context.Context, ld, rcbItemID string, update RCBUpdate) error
```

SetReportControlBlock writes selected attributes of a report control block. Only fields specified by [RCBUpdate.Fields](#func-rcbupdate-fields) are sent to the server.

This mask-based approach prevents accidental partial writes that could leave the RCB in an inconsistent state.

#### func (Client) SubscribeReport

```go
func (c *Client) SubscribeReport(ctx context.Context, rptID string, opts SubscribeReportOptions) (*ReportSubscription, error)
```

SubscribeReport creates a subscription that delivers decoded IEC 61850 reports matching the specified RptID pattern.

The caller must read from the [ReportSubscription.Reports](#func-reportsubscription-reports) channel to avoid backpressure. Overflow behavior is controlled by [SubscribeReportOptions.OverflowPolicy](#func-subscribereportoptions-overflowpolicy).

Lifecycle options (AutoEnable, GIOnSubscribe, ReserveURCB) allow the subscription to configure and enable the RCB automatically. These require LD and RCBItemID to be set in options. The caller can still configure RCBs manually via [Client.SetReportControlBlock](#func-client-setreportcontrolblock) and subscribe passively by not setting any lifecycle options.

Call [ReportSubscription.Close](#func-reportsubscription-close) when done. The subscription is also closed when the client is closed.

The context is the lifetime of the subscription, not only of this call: it bounds the setup requests (reserve, enable, GI), and when it ends afterwards, by cancellation or by its deadline, the subscription is closed as by [ReportSubscription.Close](#func-reportsubscription-close), including the remote cleanup. Pass a context that lives as long as the subscription should; with a timeout context around the call (context.WithTimeout followed by defer cancel()) the subscription closes when the calling function returns or when the timeout passes.

Lifecycle operations are not atomic. If subscription setup fails partway through, some RCB state (e.g., Resv, DatSet) may already have been changed on the server. Rollback is best-effort: the library attempts to undo prior writes, but network or server errors during cleanup are logged and otherwise ignored.

SetReportControlBlock write ordering: configuration fields are written first, RptEna is always written last. This is an IEC 61850 invariant — the library does not promise atomic RCB updates. See [Client.SetReportControlBlock](#func-client-setreportcontrolblock) for details.

#### func (Client) Tree

```go
func (c *Client) Tree(ctx context.Context) (*ModelNode, error)
```

Tree builds the full IEC 61850 model tree from the server. This performs multiple MMS GetNameList calls to discover the complete hierarchy: logical devices → logical nodes → data objects/attributes.

The returned root [ModelNode](#type-modelnode) is a synthetic container (Name="root", empty Reference) whose Children are the logical device nodes. It does not represent a real IEC 61850 object.

The tree merges structure across functional constraints: the same data object path may appear under multiple FCs (e.g., ST and MX), and the tree returns it as a single node. Enable [TreeOptions.IncludeFCs](#func-treeoptions-includefcs) to annotate each node with its observed FCs. Without FC annotation, a returned node is a browse view, not a directly readable reference — callers must choose an FC before reading or writing.

The tree includes all data objects and attributes discovered from the MMS variable names. For type information, use [Client.GetVariableType](#func-client-getvariabletype) on individual nodes.

This operation may be slow on servers with large models.

#### func (Client) TreeWithOptions

```go
func (c *Client) TreeWithOptions(ctx context.Context, opts TreeOptions) (*ModelNode, error)
```

TreeWithOptions builds the IEC 61850 model tree with configurable filtering and annotation.

Like [Client.Tree](#func-client-tree), the returned tree merges structure across functional constraints. Use [TreeOptions.IncludeFCs](#func-treeoptions-includefcs) to annotate nodes with their observed FCs so that callers can determine which FCs are valid for each node before performing read/write operations.

See [Client.Tree](#func-client-tree) for the simpler zero-options variant.

#### func (Client) TriggerGI

```go
func (c *Client) TriggerGI(ctx context.Context, ld, rcbItemID string) error
```

TriggerGI triggers a General Interrogation on a report control block.

For BRCBs, this writes GI=true to the RCB. The server responds by sending a report containing all data set members with reason=GI.

For URCBs, the same mechanism applies but the RCB must be enabled and reserved (if applicable) first.

#### func (Client) Write

```go
func (c *Client) Write(ctx context.Context, ref Ref, value *mms.Value) error
```

Write writes a single IEC 61850 data attribute.

The ref must include LD, LN, FC, and a path to the target data attribute. The value is written as-is to the MMS layer.

Returns an error if the write is rejected by the server.

#### func (Client) WriteDataSet

```go
func (c *Client) WriteDataSet(ctx context.Context, ld, dsName string, values []*mms.Value) ([]error, error)
```

WriteDataSet is SetDataSetValues (IEC 61850-7-2 13.3.3): it writes values to the members of the data set dsName of ld in one MMS Write of the named variable list (IEC 61850-8-1 8.1.3.4.3.3), values\[i] to member i. A dsName beginning with "@" addresses a non-persistent data set of the association (see [Client.CreateDataSet](#func-client-createdataset)).

The returned slice has one entry per member: nil when the member was written, a [\*DataAccessError](#type-dataaccesserror) with the server's code otherwise. The error is non-nil when the request itself failed.

#### func (Client) WriteMultiple

```go
func (c *Client) WriteMultiple(ctx context.Context, requests []WriteRequest) ([]WriteResult, error)
```

WriteMultiple writes multiple IEC 61850 data attributes in a single MMS request.

Each request must include a valid ref (LD, LN, FC, path) and a non-nil value. Results are returned in the same order as the input requests. Per-item errors are reported in [WriteResult.Err](#func-writeresult-err) as a [\*DataAccessError](#type-dataaccesserror).

Duplicate refs are preserved: if the same ref appears multiple times, each write is sent in order. The final server-side value is the last successful write.

Mixed-domain and mixed-FC writes are supported: requests may span different logical devices and functional constraints within a single call. Write order is preserved.

If the MMS request itself fails, a non-nil error is returned and the result slice is nil.

### type ClientOptions

```go
type ClientOptions struct {
	// Logger, when non-nil, enables structured logging for IEC 61850
	// operations. When nil (the default), no logging is emitted.
	Logger *slog.Logger

	// Strictness controls validation behavior.
	Strictness StrictnessOptions

	// Cache controls the client-side caching strategy for model
	// discovery results (logical devices, logical nodes, data
	// objects, tree). The default ([CacheNone]) disables caching.
	Cache CacheStrategy

	// IEDName, when non-empty, is the IED identifier prefix used by
	// the target server to form MMS domain names. See [DialOptions.IEDName].
	IEDName string

	// Clock stamps the T member (time and TimeQuality) of Operate,
	// SelectWithValue and Cancel (IEC 61850-7-2 20.5.2.5). Nil is
	// [SystemClock]: the host time, "clock not synchronised". A
	// per-call OperateParams.TQuality or CancelParams.TQuality
	// overrides the clock's quality.
	Clock Clock

	// FileLimits bounds what [Client.ReadFile] and [Client.DownloadFile]
	// accept from the server. The zero value uses the defaults.
	FileLimits FileLimits

	// JournalLimits bounds what [Client.ReadJournalAll] and
	// [Client.ReadJournalAfterAll] accumulate from the server. The zero
	// value uses the defaults.
	JournalLimits JournalLimits
}
```

ClientOptions configures an IEC 61850 client created via [NewClient](#func-newclient) from an existing [mms.Client](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Client).

### type Clock

```go
type Clock interface {
	// Now returns the current time. Only the wall-clock reading is
	// used.
	Now() time.Time

	// Quality returns the TimeQuality of the times Now returns.
	Quality() TimeQuality
}
```

Clock is the source of the protocol timestamps the client and server send: the time and the TimeQuality of IEC 61850-7-2 TimeStamp (LeapSecondsKnown, ClockFailure, ClockNotSynchronized, TimeAccuracy), which IEC 61850-8-1 encodes as the last octet of a UtcTime.

A Clock stamps values only. Timers (sboTimeout, the operTm wait, IntgPd, BufTm, ResvTms, the reservation release) run on the Go runtime's monotonic clock and never call a Clock, so stepping the wall clock (an NTP or PTP correction, a fake clock in a test) does not fire, shorten or stretch them.

Implementations must be safe for concurrent use. Now is called once per stamped value and Quality right after it; both should return quickly (cache a sync status that is expensive to read).

See [SystemClock](#type-systemclock) for the default and [ClockWithQuality](#func-clockwithquality) to attach a synchronisation status to the host clock.

#### func ClockWithQuality

```go
func ClockWithQuality(quality func() TimeQuality) Clock
```

ClockWithQuality returns a [Clock](#type-clock) that reads the time from [time.Now](https://pkg.go.dev/time#Now) and the TimeQuality from quality, called once per stamped value. Nil quality is [SystemClock](#type-systemclock).

It is the hook for a synchronisation-status source; the library has no OS integration of its own. An application maps its source to a TimeQuality, typically from a status it refreshes in the background rather than querying per call:

  - chrony: "chronyc -c tracking" gives the leap status (field 14, "Not synchronised" sets ClockNotSynchronized) and the system time offset and root dispersion, from which TimeAccuracy follows as the number of fraction bits n with 2^-n s at or above the error bound.
  - ptp4l: pmc "GET TIME\_STATUS\_NP" (gmPresent, master offset) and "GET PARENT\_DATA\_SET" (grandmaster clockClass: 6 is locked to a primary reference, holdover and free-running classes are not synchronised); a valid currentUtcOffset from "GET TIME\_PROPERTIES\_DATA\_SET" sets LeapSecondsKnown. phc2sys keeps the system clock on the PTP hardware clock.
  - NTP (ntpd, systemd-timesyncd): the kernel's adjtimex(2) status (TIME\_ERROR, STA\_UNSYNC) and maxerror give ClockNotSynchronized and TimeAccuracy.

A clock hardware fault the source reports sets ClockFailure.

### type CommandTermination

```go
type CommandTermination struct {
	// Ref is the controlled object, as passed to [Client.OperateWait].
	Ref string

	// Oper is the Oper value the server reported.
	Oper *mms.Value

	// LastApplError is set for a negative termination.
	LastApplError *LastApplError
}
```

CommandTermination is the outcome a server reports after it executed an operate of a control with enhanced security (IEC 61850-8-1, CommandTermination): an InformationReport of the Oper attribute, preceded by a LastApplError when the operation failed.

#### func (CommandTermination) Positive

```go
func (t *CommandTermination) Positive() bool
```

Positive reports whether the operation completed successfully.

### type ConnectionEvent

```go
type ConnectionEvent struct{}
```

ConnectionEvent is passed to [ServerOptions.OnConnect](#func-serveroptions-onconnect) and [ServerOptions.OnDisconnect](#func-serveroptions-ondisconnect) callbacks.

The event currently provides no connection-specific context because the underlying MMS layer does not expose the [mms.ServerConn](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#ServerConn) at the transport-accept boundary. Future versions may add a connection identifier or authentication token when the MMS API supports it.

### type ControlError

```go
type ControlError struct {
	// Ref is the IEC 61850 object reference of the controlled object.
	Ref string

	// Operation is the control operation that failed (e.g. "operate",
	// "select", "cancel").
	Operation string

	// AddCause is the additional cause reported by the server via
	// LastApplError, if available. Zero means unknown or not read.
	AddCause AddCause

	// LastApplError is the LastApplError the server reported for the
	// failed control write or in a negative CommandTermination; nil when
	// it sent none.
	LastApplError *LastApplError

	// Wrapped is the underlying error.
	Wrapped error
}
```

ControlError is a typed error for control operation failures. It captures the object reference, the operation attempted, and the server-reported additional cause when available.

#### func (ControlError) Error

```go
func (e *ControlError) Error() string
```

#### func (ControlError) Unwrap

```go
func (e *ControlError) Unwrap() []error
```

Unwrap returns a slice of errors so that [errors.Is](https://pkg.go.dev/errors#Is) matches both the operation-specific sentinel (e.g. ErrOperateFailed) and the wrapped cause, if any.

### type ControlHandler

```go
type ControlHandler struct {
	// SelectTimeout overrides the select timeout for this control
	// object: the selection is released this long after a successful
	// Select or SelectWithValue. Zero uses the model's CF sboTimeout
	// (milliseconds, IEC 61850-7-3) when it is set and not zero, and
	// [DefaultSelectTimeout] otherwise.
	SelectTimeout time.Duration

	// OnSelect is called when a client issues a Select (SBO, a Read of
	// SBO) or SelectWithValue (SBOw) request. Return nil to accept the
	// select, or an error (preferably wrapping [ErrSelectFailed]
	// with an [AddCause]) to deny it. A denied Select reads back an empty
	// string (IEC 61850-8-1 20.5.5).
	//
	// If nil, selects are accepted unconditionally.
	OnSelect func(ctx context.Context, req ControlRequest) error

	// OnOperate is called when a client issues an Operate request: at
	// once, or for a time activated operate (non-zero OperTm in the
	// future) when OperTm is reached. Return nil to accept the operate,
	// or an error (preferably wrapping [ErrOperateFailed] with an
	// [AddCause]) to deny it.
	//
	// If nil, operates are accepted and the server applies a default
	// for simple status controls: ctlVal is written to $ST$..$stVal when
	// it fits stVal's type (BOOLEAN to Dbpos for a DPC: on 10, off 01),
	// with t, and origin and ctlNum when the DO has them; Process adds
	// the process response (travel through intermediate-state, operation
	// counter, position-reached).
	OnOperate func(ctx context.Context, req ControlRequest) error

	// OnCancel is called when a client issues a Cancel request that
	// is accepted (no other client holds the selection, the parameters
	// match the selection). Return nil to accept the cancellation, or an
	// error to deny.
	//
	// If nil, cancels are accepted unconditionally.
	OnCancel func(ctx context.Context, req ControlRequest) error

	// OnExecute, for controls with enhanced security, runs after a
	// successful operate and before the CommandTermination: nil sends a
	// positive termination, an error a negative one with a LastApplError
	// whose AddCause is the error's [ControlError.AddCause] (unknown
	// otherwise). It runs in the background with the request's values,
	// ending when the server closes, and, when the model's CF
	// operTimeout (milliseconds) is set, at that timeout: an error once
	// the timeout passed gives AddCause time-limit-over. Nil means the
	// operate completes with OnOperate. The control stays in execution
	// until OnExecute returns, and leaves it before the termination is
	// sent: meanwhile another Oper, SBOw or Cancel gets
	// command-already-in-execution (IEC 61850-7-2 20.3.3, Table 47).
	OnExecute func(ctx context.Context, req ControlRequest) error

	// CheckInterlock is the interlocking check, an operative test (IEC
	// 61850-7-2 20.2.1, 20.5.2.7): called at SelectWithValue and at
	// Operate (for a time activated operate when operTm is reached) when
	// the request's Check has interlock-check, after the CILO binding of
	// Interlocking passed. Return nil to allow the command; an error
	// refuses it with AddCause blocked-by-interlocking (Table 54) unless
	// it is a [*ControlError] with another AddCause. An Operate refused
	// by a test gets a negative response and, for a time activated
	// operate, a negative termination; nil ignores the Check bit (20.5.2.7).
	CheckInterlock func(ctx context.Context, req ControlRequest) error

	// CheckSynchro is the synchrocheck, a dynamic test (IEC 61850-7-2
	// 20.2.1): called at Operate, after the operative tests, when the
	// request's Check has synchrocheck and the RSYN binding of
	// Synchrocheck released. It may block until synchronism; its context
	// ends at SynchroTimeout and at a Cancel. An error refuses with
	// AddCause blocked-by-synchrocheck (Table 54) unless it is a
	// [*ControlError] with another AddCause; a Cancel gives
	// abortion-by-cancel. Nil ignores the Check bit (20.5.2.7).
	CheckSynchro func(ctx context.Context, req ControlRequest) error

	// SynchroTimeout is the time limit of the synchrocheck: how long the
	// RSYN binding waits for Rel.stVal TRUE, and the deadline of
	// CheckSynchro's context. Zero checks the RSYN release once.
	SynchroTimeout time.Duration

	// Interlocking names the CILO logical node of this control: "CILO1"
	// in the control's logical device, or "LD/CILO1". When the request's
	// Check has interlock-check, a close (ctlVal TRUE) needs
	// EnaCls.stVal TRUE and an open (FALSE) EnaOpn.stVal TRUE (IEC
	// 61850-7-4 CILO), else blocked-by-interlocking. A ctlVal that is not
	// BOOLEAN is not gated. RegisterControl refuses a CILO the model has
	// not.
	Interlocking string

	// Synchrocheck names the RSYN logical node of this control ("RSYN1"
	// or "LD/RSYN1"). When the request's Check has synchrocheck, the
	// Operate waits up to SynchroTimeout for Rel.stVal TRUE (IEC
	// 61850-7-4 RSYN), else blocked-by-synchrocheck. RegisterControl
	// refuses an RSYN the model has not.
	Synchrocheck string

	// Process, when set, models the process response of the default
	// operate (no OnOperate): see [ProcessResponse]. Nil mirrors ctlVal
	// into stVal.
	Process *ProcessResponse

	// MaxOperDelay bounds a time activated operate: an Operate whose
	// operTm is further than this in the future is refused with AddCause
	// time-limit-over, and the control stays as it was. Zero or less
	// means [DefaultMaxOperDelay].
	MaxOperDelay time.Duration
}
```

ControlHandler defines the server-side callbacks for a controllable data object. Implement the methods relevant to the control model; unset (nil) handlers use default accept/reject behavior.

All handler methods receive a context from the MMS layer and a [ControlRequest](#type-controlrequest) describing the command. A callback refuses with an error, preferably a [\*ControlError](#type-controlerror) with an [AddCause](#type-addcause); it is reported in the LastApplError (IEC 61850-8-1 20.11; a ControlError whose LastApplError has a non-zero Error sets that Error code) and the write gets the DataAccessError the error carries (ErrWriteAccessDenied and the other Err\* write sentinels, or an [\*mms.DataAccessError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#DataAccessError)), else the one of IEC 61850-8-1 Table 87 for its AddCause: temporarily-unavailable for object-already-selected, command-already-in-execution and locked-by-other-client, object-access-denied otherwise (as libiec61850 answers).

Callbacks are not called with the control's lock held; a control is in one state at a time (IEC 61850-7-2 Table 47), so OnOperate and OnExecute of one control never overlap.

### type ControlRequest

```go
type ControlRequest struct {
	// Ref is the IEC 61850 object reference of the controlled object.
	Ref string

	// Operation is "operate", "select", or "cancel".
	Operation string

	// CtlVal is the control value; nil for a Select (SBO).
	CtlVal *mms.Value

	// Origin is the command originator.
	Origin Origin

	// CtlNum is the control sequence number.
	CtlNum uint8

	// OperTm is the activation time of a time activated operate; zero
	// for an immediate command (operTm absent or all zero, IEC 61850-8-1
	// 20.10.2.2).
	OperTm time.Time

	// Test indicates whether this is a test command.
	Test bool

	// Check contains synchrocheck/interlockCheck bits.
	Check CheckConditions
}
```

ControlRequest contains the decoded parameters from a client control command (Operate, Select, or Cancel).

### type CtlModel

```go
type CtlModel int
```

CtlModel represents the IEC 61850 control model (ctlModel attribute). It determines whether the controllable data object uses direct operation, select-before-operate, or enhanced security variants.

```go
const (
	// CtlModelStatusOnly means the data object is not controllable.
	CtlModelStatusOnly CtlModel = 0

	// CtlModelDirectNormal is direct-operate with normal security.
	// The client writes to Oper without a prior Select.
	CtlModelDirectNormal CtlModel = 1

	// CtlModelSBONormal is select-before-operate with normal security.
	// The client reads SBO (select), then writes to Oper.
	CtlModelSBONormal CtlModel = 2

	// CtlModelDirectEnhanced is direct-operate with enhanced security.
	// Like CtlModelDirectNormal, but the server validates origin,
	// ctlNum, and timestamps for command verification.
	CtlModelDirectEnhanced CtlModel = 3

	// CtlModelSBOEnhanced is select-before-operate with enhanced
	// security. The client writes to SBOw (select-with-value), then
	// writes to Oper, with full origin/ctlNum/timestamp verification.
	CtlModelSBOEnhanced CtlModel = 4
)
```
