### type DialOptions

```go
type DialOptions struct {
	// MMS holds the underlying MMS dial options. These are passed
	// through to [iso.Dial] via [iso.WithClientDialOptions].
	MMS mms.DialOptions

	// Logger, when non-nil, enables structured logging for IEC 61850
	// operations. When nil (the default), no logging is emitted.
	//
	// When [DialOptions.MMS].Logger is also nil, this logger is passed
	// through to the underlying [mms.Client]. ISO transport logging
	// ([iso.WithLogger]) is independent and is not set from here.
	Logger *slog.Logger

	// Strictness controls validation behavior.
	Strictness StrictnessOptions

	// Cache controls the client-side caching strategy for model
	// discovery results. The default ([CacheNone]) disables caching.
	Cache CacheStrategy

	// IEDName, when non-empty, is the IED identifier prefix used by
	// the target server to form MMS domain names.
	//
	// Compliant IEC 61850-8-1 servers form MMS domain names by
	// concatenating the IED name and the LD instance name (e.g.
	// IEDName="InteropIED" + LDInst="InteropLD" →
	// domain="InteropIEDInteropLD"). When IEDName is set, the
	// client automatically strips the prefix when reporting logical
	// device names and prepends it when making MMS requests, so
	// callers can always use the bare LD instance name.
	IEDName string

	// Retry controls how [Dial] retries a failed connection attempt; it
	// is passed to [iso.WithRetry], so one attempt covers the TCP connect,
	// the COTP handshake and the MMS association, and errors another
	// attempt cannot fix (see [mms.IsRetryable]) are returned at once.
	// Each retry is logged at Warn before RetryPolicy.OnRetry is called.
	// The zero value makes a single attempt; [mms.DefaultRetryPolicy] is
	// a sensible reconnect policy.
	Retry mms.RetryPolicy

	// Metrics, when non-nil, receives the MMS request and connection
	// events of the client (see [mms.Metrics]). It is a convenience field
	// equivalent to MMS.Metrics, which takes precedence when both are set.
	// Either is called under a recover: a call that does not return
	// normally is logged with its stack at error level and loses that
	// event.
	Metrics mms.Metrics

	// MaxTPDULength is the COTP TPDU size proposed in the connection
	// request, passed to [iso.WithMaxTPDULength]. Zero means the go-mms
	// default, 1024 octets; 65531 omits the parameter (the RFC 1006
	// default). Valid values are 128..65531.
	MaxTPDULength int

	// Dialer, when non-nil, opens the TCP connection in place of a zero
	// [net.Dialer]'s DialContext; it is passed to [iso.WithDialer]. Use it
	// for a destination allowlist checked against the resolved IP, a
	// proxy, custom socket options, or an in-memory transport in tests.
	// It is called once per attempt (see Retry) with network "tcp" and
	// the address given to [Dial]. The context carries the caller's
	// deadline and cancellation; a custom dialer must honour it. Like
	// [net.Dialer], it returns a non-nil connection exactly when the error
	// is nil: a connection returned with an error is closed, and a nil
	// connection with a nil error fails the dial. The returned connection
	// is owned and closed by the client. An error it returns is wrapped by
	// [Dial] and can be matched with [errors.Is]. Nil keeps the default
	// dialer.
	Dialer func(ctx context.Context, network, addr string) (net.Conn, error)

	// Clock stamps the T member of control commands (see
	// [ClientOptions.Clock]). Nil is [SystemClock].
	Clock Clock

	// FileLimits bounds the file services of the client (see
	// [ClientOptions.FileLimits]). The zero value uses the defaults.
	FileLimits FileLimits

	// JournalLimits bounds what the client accumulates from a journal
	// (see [ClientOptions.JournalLimits]). The zero value uses the
	// defaults.
	JournalLimits JournalLimits
}
```

DialOptions configures an IEC 61850 client connection established via [Dial](#func-dial).

```go
	// Pattern is matched against the object reference (without FC
	// suffix). The matching algorithm is determined by [MatchMode].
```

### type GOOSEEngine

```go
type GOOSEEngine struct {

	// key: store-key prefix "LD/LLN0$GO$name"

}
```

GOOSEEngine publishes the GOOSE control blocks of a [Server](#type-server)'s model.

Every GoCB (SCL GSEControl in LLN0 with a GSE address) gets a [goose.Publisher](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/goose#Publisher). When a dataset member changes through [Server.SetValue](#func-server-setvalue) or an MMS client write, the engine publishes a new state if the member values differ from the last published ones.

The GoCB attributes are served over MMS under the GO functional constraint: GoEna, GoID and DatSet are writable (GoID and DatSet only while GoEna is false; every DatSet write increments ConfRev, 7-2 18.2.1.6, and one that would take it past 4294967295 is refused), all other attributes are read-only. GoID and DatSet are writable as in IEC 61850-7-2 Table 42, although the 8-1 Table 73 mapping lists them read-only.

A GoCB whose address is unconfigured (00-00-00-00-00-00, 8-1 Annex B) or not multicast, whose ConfRev is 0 (7-2 18.2.1.3) or whose dataset cannot be resolved has NdsCom TRUE and cannot be enabled. A GoCB with FixedOffs TRUE publishes the fixed-length encoding of 8-1 Annex A.3.

```go
type JournalEngine struct {

	// keyed by "ldName/journalName"
	// keyed by "ldName/<LN>$LG$<name>"

	// LCBs by LogRef

	// clock stamps integrity entries (the server's Clock); nil is
	// SystemClock. The IntgPd ticker never uses it.

	// minIntgPd is the smallest non-zero IntgPd in ms a client may
	// write (ServerOptions.MinIntegrityPeriod); 0 means no minimum.

}
```

JournalEngine is the server-side runtime journal engine. It generates journal (log) entries in response to value changes and application events, storing them in a [MemoryJournalProvider](#type-memoryjournalprovider) that backs the MMS journal services.

The engine is created by [Server.EnableJournals](#func-server-enablejournals) and attached to the server's MMS layer as the [mms.JournalProvider](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#JournalProvider).

#### func (JournalEngine) HandleLCBWrite

```go
func (e *JournalEngine) HandleLCBWrite(_ context.Context, ldName, lcbItem, attr string, val *mms.Value) error
```

HandleLCBWrite applies a client write of LCB attribute attr (IEC 61850-8-1 §17.3.4.3 SetLCBValues). While LogEna is TRUE, writes to LogRef, DatSet, TrgOps and IntgPd are rejected; a LogRef naming no existing journal and a DatSet naming no existing named variable list are rejected too. The value is committed only when the write is accepted.

#### func (JournalEngine) LogEvent

```go
func (e *JournalEngine) LogEvent(domain, journal string, occTime time.Time, vars []mms.JournalVariable) []byte
```

LogEvent records a custom application event in the specified journal. The domain is the logical device name and journal is the MMS journal name (typically "LLN0$logName"). Variables contain the data to record.

#### func (JournalEngine) LogValueWrite

```go
func (e *JournalEngine) LogValueWrite(_ context.Context, storeKey string, occTime time.Time)
```

LogValueWrite evaluates the log control blocks for a write of the value at storeKey ("ldName/itemID"). Every enabled LCB (LogEna TRUE) whose data set contains the attribute and whose trigger options the write meets journals the member value followed by its reason code (IEC 61850-7-2 §17.3.4, IEC 61850-8-1 §17.3.3.4.4). Writes outside an LCB data set are not journaled.

#### func (JournalEngine) Provider

```go
func (e *JournalEngine) Provider() *MemoryJournalProvider
```

Provider returns the underlying [MemoryJournalProvider](#type-memoryjournalprovider) used by this engine, allowing direct inspection of stored entries.

JournalEntry represents a single entry in an IEC 61850 journal (log).

### type JournalLimits

```go
type JournalLimits struct {
	// MaxEntries is the number of entries accepted; zero means
	// [DefaultMaxJournalEntries].
	MaxEntries int

	// MaxBytes is the estimated memory of the entries accepted (entry
	// IDs, tags and decoded values); zero means
	// [DefaultMaxJournalBytes].
	MaxBytes int64
}
```

JournalLimits bounds the entries [Client.ReadJournalAll](#func-client-readjournalall) and [Client.ReadJournalAfterAll](#func-client-readjournalafterall) collect over the pages of a journal. A field that is zero uses its default; a negative field means no limit. A read that goes beyond a limit is given up with an error that wraps ErrLimitExceeded. The single-page reads ([Client.ReadJournal](#func-client-readjournal), [Client.ReadJournalAfter](#func-client-readjournalafter)) are bounded by the MMS PDU size.

### type MemoryJournalProvider

```go
type MemoryJournalProvider struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

MemoryJournalProvider is a thread-safe, in-memory implementation of [mms.JournalProvider](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#JournalProvider). It stores entries per (domain, journal) pair with configurable maximum capacity. When the capacity is exceeded, the oldest entries are discarded (ring-buffer semantics).

Entry IDs are auto-assigned as monotonically increasing 8-byte big-endian integers, guaranteeing strict ordering even when multiple entries share the same OccurrenceTime. This makes cursor pagination deterministic and skip-free.

This provider is intended for testing, development, and lightweight server deployments. For production use with large journal volumes, a persistent provider backed by a database or file storage should be used instead.

#### func NewMemoryJournalProvider

```go
func NewMemoryJournalProvider(opts ...MemoryJournalOption) *MemoryJournalProvider
```

NewMemoryJournalProvider creates a new in-memory journal provider.

#### func (MemoryJournalProvider) AddEntry

```go
func (p *MemoryJournalProvider) AddEntry(domain, journal string, occTime time.Time, vars []mms.JournalVariable) []byte
```

AddEntry appends a journal entry with the given timestamp and variable data. The EntryID is assigned automatically. Returns the assigned EntryID, a copy the caller owns.

The provided variables are defensively copied so that later mutation of the caller's slice or the values within it does not corrupt the journal history.

If the journal does not exist, it is created implicitly.


EntryCount returns the number of entries in the specified journal.

### type MemoryReportBuffer

```go
type MemoryReportBuffer struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

MemoryReportBuffer is the default [ReportBuffer](#type-reportbuffer): entries in memory, bounded by a number of entries and, optionally, by their [ReportEntry.EncodedSize](#func-reportentry-encodedsize) in octets. It does not survive a restart.

A MemoryReportBuffer is not safe for concurrent use; the report engine serialises its calls.

#### func NewMemoryReportBuffer

```go
func NewMemoryReportBuffer(maxEntries, maxBytes int) *MemoryReportBuffer
```

NewMemoryReportBuffer returns an in-memory report buffer that holds at most maxEntries entries (at least 1; 0 or less means 1000) and, when maxBytes is positive, entries of at most maxBytes octets in all. When an entry is appended to a full buffer the oldest entries are discarded (IEC 61850-7-2 §17.2.3.2.2.8). The newest entry is kept even when it alone exceeds maxBytes.

### type OperateParams

```go
type OperateParams struct {
	// CtlVal is the control value to write. Required.
	// Use [BoolCtlVal], [IntCtlVal], [FloatCtlVal], [EnumCtlVal],
	// or [StringCtlVal] to construct it.
	CtlVal *mms.Value

	// Origin identifies the command originator. When nil, a default
	// Origin with OrCatRemoteControl and empty OrIdent is used.
	Origin *Origin

	// CtlNum is the control sequence number (INT8U, 0..255). All
	// commands of one control sequence carry the same ctlNum (IEC
	// 61850-7-2 20.5.2.4). Zero, with CtlNumSet false, means unset: the
	// library uses the ctlNum of the last SelectWithValue of the control
	// (Operate), or the next value of an auto-incrementing counter.
	CtlNum uint8

	// CtlNumSet sends CtlNum as given, zero included.
	CtlNumSet bool

	// OperTm is the scheduled operation time. A zero value means
	// "operate now" (no timed command); the library then sends operTm
	// all zero when the server's Oper type has it (IEC 61850-8-1
	// 20.10.2.2).
	OperTm time.Time

	// Test, when true, sets the Test bit to indicate a test command
	// that should not cause physical action.
	Test bool

	// Check specifies synchrocheck/interlockCheck conditions.
	Check CheckConditions

	// TQuality, when set, is the TimeQuality of the T member (the time
	// the command was sent, IEC 61850-7-2 20.5.2.5; IEC 61850-8-1 Table
	// 32), overriding the quality of the client's Clock. Nil sends
	// the quality of [ClientOptions.Clock] ([DialOptions.Clock]); the
	// default [SystemClock] sends "clock not synchronised", 10 bits of
	// accuracy (0x2a). Before v1.18.0 nil sent 0x0a (synchronised).
	TQuality *TimeQuality
}
```

OperateParams contains all parameters for an IEC 61850 control Operate or SelectWithValue command.

At minimum, CtlVal must be set. For enhanced security models, Origin, CtlNum, and timestamps are also required. The library fills in sensible defaults for unset fields when possible.

### type OverflowPolicy

```go
type OverflowPolicy int
```

OverflowPolicy controls what happens when a subscription's report channel is full.

#### URCB vs BRCB loss semantics {#hdr-URCB_vs_BRCB_loss_semantics}

For URCB (unbuffered) reports, report loss at the application queue level is expected and accepted — the server makes no durability promise. When OverflowDropNewest or OverflowDropOldest is used, lost reports are silently discarded and the client will not observe a gap indicator. This matches the standard URCB contract: reports are best-effort.

For BRCB (buffered) reports, application queue overflow is a different concern from the server-side BRCB buffer overflow:

  - Server-side BRCB buffer overflow occurs when the in-memory buffer (default: 1000 entries) is full, typically while no client has the BRCB enabled (it buffers in every state, IEC 61850-7-2 §17.2.3.2.3.6). The server drops the oldest entry; when that entry was not yet sent, the next delivered report has BufOvfl=true so the client knows a gap exists (§17.2.3.2.2.8).

  - Client-side application queue overflow (this type) occurs when the client's in-process channel (QueueSize) fills up while reports are being delivered. The chosen OverflowPolicy applies here; the server is unaware of this loss. For BRCB use cases that require no loss, set QueueSize large enough and consume reports promptly, or use OverflowBlock.

#### Choosing a policy {#hdr-Choosing_a_policy}

  - OverflowDropNewest: default. Safe for all uses. Report loss is visible in SeqNum gaps.
  - OverflowDropOldest: prefer fresher data; older values are discarded.
  - OverflowBlock: zero-loss delivery. While the channel is full it blocks the whole association, not only report dispatch: see below.
  - OverflowCallback: custom handling (e.g., metrics, reconnect trigger).

#### What OverflowBlock blocks {#hdr-What_OverflowBlock_blocks}

Reports are dispatched on the goroutine that reads the association, which is also the one that reads the response to every confirmed request. While an OverflowBlock subscription's channel is full, that goroutine waits for the consumer, so:

  - no report of any subscription of this client is delivered, and
  - no confirmed service of this client completes (Read, Write, a control, [Client.GetReportControlBlock](#func-client-getreportcontrolblock), [Client.TriggerGI](#func-client-triggergi), ...): each waits until the consumer has read a report, until its own context ends, or until the subscription or the client is closed.

Therefore, with OverflowBlock:

  - read the Reports channel from a goroutine that issues no request on this client, and give every request a context with a deadline;
  - do not combine it with AutoEnable and GIOnSubscribe on an RCB that can send more than QueueSize reports before [Client.SubscribeReport](#func-client-subscribereport) returns (a BRCB that replays a backlog when it is enabled): the subscription is registered before the RCB is enabled, the queue fills while the caller has no channel to read yet, and the GI request then waits until the context ends. Subscribe with AutoEnable only, start reading, then call [Client.TriggerGI](#func-client-triggergi).

```go
const (
	// OverflowDropNewest drops the incoming report when the channel
	// is full (default). A warning is logged.
	OverflowDropNewest OverflowPolicy = iota

	// OverflowDropOldest discards the oldest buffered report to
	// make room for the new one.
	OverflowDropOldest

	// OverflowBlock blocks the dispatcher until space is available.
	// Use with caution: the dispatcher is the goroutine that reads the
	// association, so this blocks all report delivery and the response
	// of every confirmed request of the client until the consumer reads
	// (see "What OverflowBlock blocks" on [OverflowPolicy]).
	OverflowBlock

	// OverflowCallback invokes the OnOverflow callback (if set)
	// and drops the report. If no callback is set, behaves like
	// [OverflowDropNewest].
	OverflowCallback
)
```

### type ProcessResponse

```go
type ProcessResponse struct {
	// TravelTime is the time the device takes to reach the commanded
	// position. For a DPC (stVal Dbpos), stVal shows intermediate-state
	// (00, IEC 61850-7-3 Dbpos) from the operate until the end position
	// is reached TravelTime later. With enhanced security the control
	// stays in WaitForChange meanwhile: the CommandTermination is
	// positive when the position is reached, negative with AddCause
	// time-limit-over when the CF operTimeout passes first, and stVal
	// then stays intermediate-state (IEC 61850-7-2 20.3.3 d). Zero
	// writes the end position at once. Ignored for a stVal that is not
	// Dbpos.
	TravelTime time.Duration

	// OpCnt names an operation counter, a data object with an integer
	// stVal (INS, such as XCBR OpCnt, IEC 61850-7-4): "LN.DO" in the
	// control's logical device or "LD/LN.DO". Its stVal is incremented
	// when an operation reaches its end position; it saturates at the
	// INT32 maximum. Empty counts nothing.
	OpCnt string

	// PositionReached refuses an Operate whose ctlVal is the position
	// stVal already shows, with AddCause position-reached (IEC 61850-7-2
	// Table 54), as an operative test.
	PositionReached bool
}
```

ProcessResponse models, for the default operate (no [ControlHandler.OnOperate](#func-controlhandler-onoperate)), the switching device behind a controllable status: only what IEC 61850 defines. It is opt-in; nil keeps the plain mirror of ctlVal into stVal.

### type Quality

```go
type Quality uint16
```

Quality represents an IEC 61850 quality bit string (13 bits).

Quality is stored as a uint16 where bit positions match the IEC 61850 standard and the C libiec61850 convention:

  - bits 0–1: Validity
  - bit 2: Overflow
  - bit 3: OutOfRange
  - bit 4: BadReference
  - bit 5: Oscillatory
  - bit 6: Failure
  - bit 7: OldData
  - bit 8: Inconsistent
  - bit 9: Inaccurate
  - bit 10: Source (substituted)
  - bit 11: Test
  - bit 12: OperatorBlocked

```go
const (
	QualityOverflow     Quality = 1 << 2
	QualityOutOfRange   Quality = 1 << 3
	QualityBadReference Quality = 1 << 4
	QualityOscillatory  Quality = 1 << 5
	QualityFailure      Quality = 1 << 6
	QualityOldData      Quality = 1 << 7
	QualityInconsistent Quality = 1 << 8
	QualityInaccurate   Quality = 1 << 9
)
```

Detail quality flags (bits 2–9).

```go
const (
	QualitySourceSubstituted Quality = 1 << 10
	QualityTest              Quality = 1 << 11
	QualityOperatorBlocked   Quality = 1 << 12
)
```

Source, test, and operator flags (bits 10–12).

#### func DecodeQuality

```go
func DecodeQuality(v *mms.Value) (Quality, error)
```

DecodeQuality decodes an IEC 61850 quality from an MMS bit string value. Returns a [DecodeError](#type-decodeerror) if the value is not a bit string.

Quality is a variable-length bit string; bits that are not conveyed take their default value, 0 (IEC 61850-8-1 8.2), so a bit string of fewer than 13 bits decodes with the missing bits clear. Before v1.17.0 a bit string shorter than 13 bits was refused.

#### func (Quality) Has

```go
func (q Quality) Has(flag Quality) bool
```

Has returns true if the specified quality flag is set.

#### func (Quality) IsGood

```go
func (q Quality) IsGood() bool
```

IsGood returns true when validity is ValidityGood and no detail quality flags are set.

#### func (Quality) String


### type RCBFieldMask

```go
type RCBFieldMask uint32
```

RCBFieldMask specifies which RCB fields to write in a [Client.SetReportControlBlock](#func-client-setreportcontrolblock) call. Only fields with the corresponding mask bit set are written to the server.

```go
const (
	RCBFieldRptID    RCBFieldMask = 1 << 0  // Write RptID
	RCBFieldRptEna   RCBFieldMask = 1 << 1  // Write RptEna
	RCBFieldDatSet   RCBFieldMask = 1 << 2  // Write DatSet
	RCBFieldOptFlds  RCBFieldMask = 1 << 3  // Write OptFlds
	RCBFieldBufTm    RCBFieldMask = 1 << 4  // Write BufTm
	RCBFieldTrgOps   RCBFieldMask = 1 << 5  // Write TrgOps
	RCBFieldIntgPd   RCBFieldMask = 1 << 6  // Write IntgPd
	RCBFieldGI       RCBFieldMask = 1 << 7  // Write GI
	RCBFieldResv     RCBFieldMask = 1 << 8  // Write Resv (URCB)
	RCBFieldPurgeBuf RCBFieldMask = 1 << 9  // Write PurgeBuf (BRCB)
	RCBFieldEntryID  RCBFieldMask = 1 << 10 // Write EntryID (BRCB)
	RCBFieldResvTms  RCBFieldMask = 1 << 11 // Write ResvTms (BRCB)
)
```

RCB field mask constants for [RCBUpdate](#type-rcbupdate).

```go

```

ReasonCode represents the reason for inclusion of a data set member in a report.

```go
const (
	ReasonDataChanged    ReasonCode = 1 << 0 // Included due to data change
	ReasonQualityChanged ReasonCode = 1 << 1 // Included due to quality change
	ReasonDataUpdate     ReasonCode = 1 << 2 // Included due to data update
	ReasonIntegrity      ReasonCode = 1 << 3 // Included due to integrity scan
	ReasonGI             ReasonCode = 1 << 4 // Included due to GI

	ReasonApplicationTrigger ReasonCode = 1 << 5
```

### type Ref

```go
type Ref struct {
	// LD is the logical device name.
	LD string
	// LN is the logical node name (e.g., "LLN0", "GGIO1").
	LN string
	// Path contains the data object / data attribute path components.
	// Empty when the reference points to a logical node.
	Path []string
	// FC is the functional constraint. Empty when not specified.
	FC FunctionalConstraint
}
```

Ref is a parsed IEC 61850 object reference.

An IEC 61850 object reference identifies a node in the data model hierarchy: LogicalDevice / LogicalNode . DataObject . DataAttribute. An optional functional constraint can be appended in brackets.

Format: LD/LN.DO.DA\[FC]

A Ref may represent different levels of the hierarchy:

  - LD-only (LN empty, no path) — identifies a logical device for browsing and GetNameList operations. Not all operations accept LD-only refs; read/write require at least LN + FC.
  - LN-level (LN set, no path) — identifies a logical node.
  - Object-level (LN set, path present) — identifies a data object or data attribute.

Examples:

	simpleIOGenericIO/GGIO1.Ind1.stVal[ST]
	simpleIOGenericIO/GGIO1.Ind1.stVal
	simpleIOGenericIO/LLN0

#### func ParseRef

```go
func ParseRef(s string) (Ref, error)
```

ParseRef parses an IEC 61850 object reference string.

Accepted formats:

	LD/LN.DO.DA[FC]   — full reference with functional constraint
	LD/LN.DO.DA        — reference without FC
	LD/LN              — logical node reference
	LD                 — logical device reference (LN will be empty)

Returns a [\*ReferenceError](#type-referenceerror) wrapping ErrInvalidReference on malformed input.

The parser accepts references of any reasonable length. Use [ParseRefStrict](#func-parserefstrict) to enforce the conservative 129-character limit inspired by IEC 61850-7-2 VisibleString129.

Unknown FC values (not in the standard set) are accepted. Use [StrictnessOptions.RejectUnknownFC](#func-strictnessoptions-rejectunknownfc) at call sites or [FunctionalConstraint.IsValid](#func-functionalconstraint-isvalid) for semantic FC validation.

#### func ParseRefStrict

```go
func ParseRefStrict(s string) (Ref, error)
```

ParseRefStrict is like [ParseRef](#func-parseref) but enforces a maximum reference length of 129 characters, inspired by the IEC 61850-7-2 MMS VisibleString129 type for ObjectReference attributes, and the rules of [Ref.ValidateStrict](#func-ref-validatestrict) (since v1.17.0).

#### func RefFromMMS

```go
func RefFromMMS(domain mms.DomainID, itemID mms.ItemID) (Ref, error)
```

RefFromMMS constructs a Ref from an MMS domain ID and item ID.

The item ID is expected to follow the IEC 61850 MMS mapping convention: LN$FC$path$components. The FC is extracted from the second $-delimited segment.

Unknown FCs are accepted and stored as-is. This matches the library's "accept by default, reject via strictness" philosophy. Use [StrictnessOptions.RejectUnknownFC](#func-strictnessoptions-rejectunknownfc) at call sites to enforce stricter validation.

Returns an error for empty domain or empty segments within the item ID.

#### func (Ref) Child

```go
func (r Ref) Child(name string) (Ref, error)
```

Child returns a new reference with name appended to the path. Returns an error if r has no logical node (LD-only), if name is empty, or if name contains separator characters (/, ., $, \[, ]).

#### func (Ref) Depth

```go
func (r Ref) Depth() int
```

Depth returns the depth of the reference in the hierarchy.

  - 0: zero-value ref (empty LD)
  - 1: LD only
  - 2: LD/LN
  - 3+: LD/LN + path components (depth = 2 + len(Path))

#### func (Ref) HasPath

```go
func (r Ref) HasPath() bool
```

HasPath reports whether the reference includes a data object or data attribute path.

#### func (Ref) IsLD

```go
func (r Ref) IsLD() bool
```

IsLD reports whether the reference points to a logical device only.

#### func (Ref) IsLN

```go
func (r Ref) IsLN() bool
```

IsLN reports whether the reference points to a logical node (no path).

#### func (Ref) IsObject

```go
func (r Ref) IsObject() bool
```

IsObject reports whether the reference points to a data object or data attribute (LN set with at least one path component).

#### func (Ref) ObjectReference

```go
func (r Ref) ObjectReference() string
```

ObjectReference returns the reference formatted without the FC bracket suffix.

#### func (Ref) Parent

```go
func (r Ref) Parent() (Ref, bool)
```

Parent returns the parent reference. For a DA reference, this returns the parent DO or LN. Returns false if r is already at the top level (LD-only).

The functional constraint is preserved when the returned parent still refers to a logical node or object path. When the parent is LD-only, the FC is dropped because LD\[FC] is not a meaningful IEC 61850 reference shape.

#### func (Ref) String

```go
func (r Ref) String() string
```

String returns the canonical IEC 61850 object reference string.

#### func (Ref) ToMMS

```go
func (r Ref) ToMMS() (domain mms.DomainID, itemID mms.ItemID, err error)
```

ToMMS converts the reference to MMS domain and item ID.

Calls [Ref.Validate](#func-ref-validate) before conversion. Requires a valid FC when the reference includes a path.

LN-level refs without FC (e.g., Ref{LD:"LD1", LN:"LLN0"}) produce a bare item ID of "LLN0". This is used for GetNameList and other browse-oriented MMS operations. It is not the normal read/write mapping — MMS read/write at the LN level is a special IEC 61850 convention that returns the complete named-variable subtree. Normal attribute access requires FC-qualified refs.

Examples:

	Ref{LD:"LD1", LN:"LLN0"}                                     → domain="LD1", itemID="LLN0"
	Ref{LD:"LD1", LN:"LLN0", Path:[]string{"Mod","stVal"}, FC:FCST} → domain="LD1", itemID="LLN0$ST$Mod$stVal"

#### func (Ref) Validate

```go
func (r Ref) Validate() error
```

Validate checks the structural invariants of the Ref.

Rules:

  - LD must be non-empty
  - if LN is empty, Path must also be empty
  - if LN is empty, FC must also be empty (FC requires at least LN)
  - no empty path components
  - if FC is non-empty, it must be exactly 2 characters (length check only — unknown FC values are accepted; use [FunctionalConstraint.IsValid](#func-functionalconstraint-isvalid) for semantic validation)
  - components must not contain separators (/, ., $, \[, ])

#### func (Ref) ValidateStrict

```go
func (r Ref) ValidateStrict() error
```

ValidateStrict checks r against the name rules of the standard on top of [Ref.Validate](#func-ref-validate): every name uses A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and \_ (IEC 61850-7-2 22.2), the LD name and the part after "/" (without FC) have at most 64 characters (IEC 61850-7-2 Table 4), and the MMS item ID (LN$FC$DO$DA, with an FC of two characters when r has none) at most 64 (IEC 61850-8-1 8.1.3.2.2).

#### func (Ref) WithFC

```go
func (r Ref) WithFC(fc FunctionalConstraint) Ref
```

WithFC returns a copy of r with the functional constraint set to fc.

### type ReportBuffer

```go
type ReportBuffer interface {
	// Append stores e as the newest entry. e.ID is greater than the ID
	// of every entry in the buffer. To make room, the buffer discards
	// its oldest entries and returns them, oldest first; it never
	// discards e itself unless it cannot store it at all.
	Append(e ReportEntry) (discarded []ReportEntry)

	// After returns the oldest entry whose ID is greater than id.
	After(id uint64) (ReportEntry, bool)

	// Get returns the entry with the given ID.
	Get(id uint64) (ReportEntry, bool)

	// Oldest and Newest return the oldest and the newest entry.
	Oldest() (ReportEntry, bool)
	Newest() (ReportEntry, bool)

	// Remove deletes the entry with the given ID, if present.
	Remove(id uint64)

	// Purge deletes every entry (IEC 61850-7-2 §17.2.2.14).
	Purge()

	// Len returns the number of entries.
	Len() int
}
```

ReportBuffer stores the entries of one report control block in creation order: the queue of a URCB and the buffer of a BRCB (IEC 61850-7-2 §17.2.2.15, §17.2.3.2.3.6).

The report engine owns the buffer: it calls the methods with the RCB's lock held, one buffer per RCB, so an implementation need not be safe for concurrent use. It assigns the entry IDs, keeps track of what was sent and sets BufOvfl from the entries [ReportBuffer.Append](#func-reportbuffer-append) discards.

The default is [NewMemoryReportBuffer](#func-newmemoryreportbuffer) with 1000 entries and no byte limit; [ServerOptions.NewReportBuffer](#func-serveroptions-newreportbuffer) installs another one.

An implementation that cannot keep an entry (a full disk, for a persistent one) returns it from Append as discarded, so the client learns of the loss through BufOvfl. A buffer that already holds entries when [Server.EnableReports](#func-server-enablereports) runs continues them: new entry IDs follow the newest one, and GI entries in it are not sent again.

### type ReportControlBlock

```go
type ReportControlBlock struct {
	// Reference is a display-only pseudo-reference derived from the
	// MMS item ID by replacing '$' with '.' (e.g. "LD/LLN0.BR.brcb01").
	// This is not a proper IEC 61850 object reference because BR/RP
	// is a functional constraint, not a path component. Use the LD
	// and MMS item ID from the original [Client.GetReportControlBlock]
	// call for programmatic access.
	Reference string

	// Type is BRCB or URCB.
	Type RCBType

	// RptID is the report identifier.
	RptID string

	// RptEna indicates whether the report is enabled.
	RptEna bool

	// DatSet is the data set reference.
	DatSet string

	// ConfRev is the configuration revision number.
	ConfRev uint32

	// OptFlds is the optional fields bit mask.
	OptFlds OptFlds

	// BufTm is the buffer time in milliseconds.
	BufTm uint32

	// SqNum is the current sequence number.
	SqNum uint32

	// TrgOps is the trigger options bit mask.
	TrgOps TrgOps

	// IntgPd is the integrity period in milliseconds.
	IntgPd uint32

	// GI indicates a general interrogation request.
	GI bool

	// Resv is the reservation flag (URCB only).
	Resv bool

	// ResvTms is the reservation time in seconds (BRCB only, optional;
	// IEC 61850-7-2 §17.2.2.17: -1 reserved by configuration, 0 not
	// reserved).
	ResvTms int32

	// EntryID is the entry identifier (BRCB only).
	EntryID []byte

	// PurgeBuf indicates a purge buffer request (BRCB only).
	PurgeBuf bool

	// Owner is the client owner identifier (optional, edition 2+).
	Owner []byte
}
```

ReportControlBlock holds the decoded attributes of a report control block read from a server.

### type ReportEngine

```go
type ReportEngine struct {

	// maxPDU bounds the encoded size of one InformationReport; longer
	// reports are segmented (IEC 61850-7-2 §17.2.3.2.2.5).

	// clock stamps TimeOfEntry (the server's Clock); nil is
	// SystemClock. BufTm and IntgPd timers never use it.

	// keyed by "ldName/rcbItemID"

	// life ends when Stop is called; every background report send
	// derives its context from it (see sendContext).

	// clk runs the BufTm timers; TimeOfEntry comes from clock.

	// newBuffer returns the buffer of an RCB (ServerOptions.NewReportBuffer);
	// nil or a nil result is the default MemoryReportBuffer.

	// minIntgPd is the smallest non-zero IntgPd in ms a client may
	// write (ServerOptions.MinIntegrityPeriod); 0 means no minimum.

}
```

ReportEngine is the server-side runtime report engine. It monitors value changes in the [servermodel.ValueStore](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/internal/servermodel#ValueStore) and generates IEC 61850 InformationReports to connected clients based on RCB configuration (trigger options, optional fields, dataset bindings).

The engine is created by [Server.EnableReports](#func-server-enablereports) and runs until the server is shut down or [ReportEngine.Stop](#func-reportengine-stop) is called.

#### Ownership and delivery {#hdr-Ownership_and_delivery}

An RCB instance is owned by one client at a time and only that client receives its reports (IEC 61850-7-2 §17.2.1). A URCB is reserved by Resv=TRUE or implicitly by RptEna=TRUE (§17.2.4.5); a BRCB is reserved by the client that enables it (Table 37 c3). While reserved, writes by other clients are answered with temporarily-unavailable (IEC 61850-8-1 §8.1.3.4.4.2). When the owning association is lost the RCB is disabled and released (§17.2.2.5 Figure 24, §17.2.4.4).

Each enabled RCB has one delivery goroutine that formats and sends its entries in creation order (§17.2.3.2.3.5), so buffered (replayed) and live reports never overtake each other and SqNum is contiguous.

A BRCB buffers entries in all states (§17.2.3.2.3.6) from the moment its DatSet references an existing data set.

#### func (ReportEngine) HandleRCBWrite

```go
func (re *ReportEngine) HandleRCBWrite(ctx context.Context, ldName, rcbItemID, subfield string, val *mms.Value, conn ...*mms.ServerConn) error
```

HandleRCBWrite is called when a client writes to an RCB subfield. It validates the write against the IEC 61850-7-2 §17.2 / IEC 61850-8-1 §17.1 rules and, when accepted, commits the value to the store and triggers the runtime behaviour (enable, disable, GI, purge, resync). A rejected write leaves the store unchanged and returns an error wrapping an [mms.DataAccessError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#DataAccessError).

The optional conn identifies the MMS association that issued the write; it becomes the owner and the delivery target of the RCB. A call without conn is a local (server application) action: it is not subject to the reservation of another client, and an RCB enabled that way buffers or discards its reports but delivers none.

#### func (ReportEngine) NotifyValueChanged

```go
func (re *ReportEngine) NotifyValueChanged(_ context.Context, storeKey string)
```

NotifyValueChanged is called when a data attribute value is changed in the ValueStore. It checks every monitoring RCB (enabled URCBs, and BRCBs in all states, IEC 61850-7-2 §17.2.3.2.3.6) for relevant triggers and records report entries as needed.

#### func (ReportEngine) SetRCBBufMax

```go
func (re *ReportEngine) SetRCBBufMax(ldName, rcbItemID string, max int) bool
```

SetRCBBufMax sets the entry capacity of the named RCB's buffer, keeping its byte limit. It returns false if the RCB is not found or its buffer is not a [MemoryReportBuffer](#type-memoryreportbuffer). A lower capacity discards the oldest entries with the next entry.

#### func (ReportEngine) Stop

```go
func (re *ReportEngine) Stop()
```

Stop shuts down the report engine, stopping all integrity timers and delivery goroutines and disabling all RCBs.

### type ReportEntry

```go
type ReportEntry struct {
	// ID is the EntryID as a number; the wire EntryID is its 8-octet
	// big-endian encoding (IEC 61850-8-1 §17.2.1). IDs start at 1 and
	// increase by one for each entry the RCB creates; 0 is reserved for
	// an empty buffer (IEC 61850-7-2 §17.2.2.15).
	ID uint64

	// TimeOfEntry is the time the report handler received the first
	// internal notification of the entry (IEC 61850-7-2 §17.2.2.16).
	TimeOfEntry time.Time

	// Values, Reasons and Inclusion have one element per data set
	// member. Inclusion marks the members the report carries, Reasons
	// their reason for inclusion and Values their values; the elements
	// of members not included are unused.
	Values    []*mms.Value
	Reasons   []ReasonCode
	Inclusion []bool

	// GI marks a general-interrogation entry. It is sent once, in the
	// enable session that requested it, and is not replayed: a BRCB
	// buffers only dchg, qchg, dupd and integrity entries
	// (IEC 61850-7-2 §17.2.3.2.3.6).
	GI bool
}
```

ReportEntry is one entry of a report control block's queue: the content of one report before it is formatted (IEC 61850-7-2 §17.2.3.2.2.9).

The report engine creates entries and never changes one after it has been appended to a [ReportBuffer](#type-reportbuffer); a buffer may keep the slices as they are.

#### func (ReportEntry) EncodedSize

```go
func (e ReportEntry) EncodedSize() int
```

EncodedSize returns an upper bound of the encoded size of the entry's member values in octets: the size [MemoryReportBuffer](#type-memoryreportbuffer) counts against its byte limit. Data references and the report header are not included.

### type ReportIndication

```go
type ReportIndication struct {
	// RptID is the report identifier.
	RptID string

	// OptFlds is the optional fields mask from this report.
	OptFlds OptFlds

	// SeqNum is the sequence number (present when OptFldSeqNum is set).
	SeqNum uint32

	// SubSeqNum is the sub-sequence number for segmented reports.
	SubSeqNum uint32

	// MoreSegments indicates additional report segments follow.
	MoreSegments bool

	// DatSet is the data set reference (present when OptFldDataSet is set).
	DatSet string

	// BufOvfl indicates buffer overflow (present when OptFldBufOvfl is set).
	BufOvfl bool

	// EntryID is the entry identifier (present when OptFldEntryID is set).
	EntryID []byte

	// ConfRev is the configuration revision (present when OptFldConfRev is set).
	ConfRev uint32

	// Timestamp is the report timestamp (present when OptFldTimeStamp
	// is set). Decoded from UTCTime or BinaryTime depending on the
	// server's encoding.
	Timestamp time.Time

	// Inclusion is a bitmask indicating which data set members are
	// included in this report.
	Inclusion []bool

	// DataReferences contains data references for included members
	// (present when OptFldDataRef is set).
	DataReferences []string

	// Values contains the values for included members, in order of
	// inclusion. Only entries where Inclusion[i] is true have values.
	Values []*Value

	// ReasonCodes contains the reason for inclusion for each included
	// member (present when OptFldReasonCode is set).
	ReasonCodes []ReasonCode
}
```

ReportIndication represents a decoded IEC 61850 report received from the server via an InformationReport.

#### func DecodeReport

```go
func DecodeReport(values []*mms.Value) (*ReportIndication, error)
```

DecodeReport decodes the access results of an MMS InformationReport that carries an IEC 61850 report (the report format of IEC 61850-8-1): RptID, OptFlds, the optional fields OptFlds announces in their standard order (SeqNum, TimeOfEntry, DatSet, BufOvfl, EntryID, ConfRev, SubSeqNum and MoreSegmentsFollow), the inclusion bit string, then per included member its data reference (with OptFldDataRef), its value, and its reason for inclusion (with OptFldReasonCode).

It is for reports a caller did not receive through a subscription, such as those of a passive capture decoded with go-mms (mms.DecodeTSDU), and it is strict: a missing or nil value, a field of the wrong MMS type, an OptFlds or inclusion bit string that is not one, an inclusion bit string with more members than the values that follow can hold (checked before any member is decoded), and values left over after the last member are a \*ReportError. It keeps no state and sends nothing. A Client decoding the reports it subscribed to stays lenient about field types, as before.

### type ReportSubscription

```go
type ReportSubscription struct {

	// closed on Close; guards OverflowBlock send
	// tracks in-flight OverflowBlock delivers

	// Lifecycle state for Close() cleanup. Set during SubscribeReport.

	// RCB MMS item ID

	// Segmented report reassembly state. Protected by mu.
	// Keyed by (RptID, SeqNum) to avoid collisions when a
	// subscription pattern matches multiple report sources
	// sharing the same sequence space.

	// segBytes is the estimated size of segBuf (segmentSize); segGen
	// counts the partial reports, so that the timer of a partial report
	// that has ended does nothing; segTimer gives the partial report up
	// after segTimeout.

	// budget of segBuf; 0 = DefaultMaxSegmentBytes
	// reassembly time limit; 0 = DefaultSegmentTimeout

	// Counters of Stats.

}
```

ReportSubscription represents an active subscription to IEC 61850 reports. Reports are delivered to the channel returned by \[Reports].

Call [ReportSubscription.Close](#func-reportsubscription-close) to unsubscribe and release resources. Close is idempotent and safe to call from any goroutine.

#### func (ReportSubscription) Close

```go
func (s *ReportSubscription) Close() error
```

Close terminates the report subscription. It is idempotent and safe to call from any goroutine.

Close shuts the subscription down locally first: it is removed from the client's dispatch and the \[Reports] channel is closed, so no further report is delivered. This part never waits for the peer.

If the subscription was created with lifecycle options (AutoEnable, ReserveURCB), Close then performs best-effort remote cleanup: disable the RCB (RptEna=false), then release the URCB reservation. The cleanup is bounded: its requests are given up after 5 seconds in total, so Close returns also when the server does not answer. Remote cleanup errors are logged and never returned.

The remote cleanup needs the answers of the peer, which the client reads on the goroutine that also calls [SubscribeReportOptions.OnOverflow](#func-subscribereportoptions-onoverflow): a Close called from that callback on a subscription with lifecycle options returns only when the cleanup is given up. Close such a subscription from another goroutine.

#### func (ReportSubscription) Reports

```go
func (s *ReportSubscription) Reports() <-chan *ReportIndication
```

Reports returns a read-only channel that delivers decoded report indications. The channel is closed when the subscription is closed or the client connection is terminated.

#### func (ReportSubscription) Stats

```go
func (s *ReportSubscription) Stats() ReportSubscriptionStats
```

Stats returns the counters of the subscription. It is safe to call from any goroutine, also after Close.

### type ReportSubscriptionStats

```go
type ReportSubscriptionStats struct {
	// ReportsDropped counts the reports dropped because the Reports
	// channel was full: the incoming report with [OverflowDropNewest]
	// and [OverflowCallback], the oldest queued one with
	// [OverflowDropOldest]. [OverflowBlock] drops none.
	ReportsDropped uint64

	// PartialReportsDropped counts the segmented reports given up before
	// their last segment: beyond [SubscribeReportOptions.MaxSegmentBytes]
	// or [SubscribeReportOptions.SegmentTimeout], beyond 65536 segments,
	// or when a segment of another report arrived first.
	PartialReportsDropped uint64

	// CallbacksRecovered counts the calls of
	// [SubscribeReportOptions.OnOverflow] that did not return normally.
	CallbacksRecovered uint64
}
```

ReportSubscriptionStats counts what a [ReportSubscription](#type-reportsubscription) did not deliver. The counters only grow.

### type SVEngine

```go
type SVEngine struct {

	// key: store-key prefix "LD/LLN0$MS$name"

}
```

SVEngine publishes the multicast Sampled Values control blocks of a [Server](#type-server)'s model.

Every MSVCB (SCL SampledValueControl in LLN0 with an SMV address) gets an [sv.Publisher](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/sv#Publisher) that sends the current dataset values at SmpRate. When a dataset member changes through [Server.SetValue](#func-server-setvalue) or an MMS client write, the next samples carry the new value. For waveform data, take the publisher with [SVEngine.Publisher](#func-svengine-publisher) and feed it directly ([sv.Publisher.UpdateSample](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/sv#Publisher.UpdateSample)).

The MSVCB attributes are served over MMS under the MS functional constraint: SvEna, MsvID, DatSet, SmpRate, OptFlds and SmpMod are writable (all but SvEna only while SvEna is false; a DatSet change increments ConfRev); ConfRev, DstAddress and noASDU are read-only. A change that would take ConfRev past 4294967295 (INT32U) is refused, and SvEna TRUE is refused while SmpRate and SmpMod select more than [SVOptions.MaxSamplesPerSecond](#func-svoptions-maxsamplespersecond). Unicast SV (USVCB) is not supported.


ControlBlocks returns the references ("LD/LLN0$MS$name") of all MSVCBs.


SetEnabled sets SvEna of an MSVCB, exactly like an MMS client write.

