### type SVOptions

```go
type SVOptions struct {
	// Transport sends the SV frames (required). Use [sv.Open] for a
	// network interface or a [sv.Hub] port for tests.
	Transport sv.Transport

	// StartDisabled leaves SvEna false for every MSVCB; clients (or
	// [SVEngine.SetEnabled]) enable publishing. By default every MSVCB
	// with a valid address and dataset publishes immediately.
	StartDisabled bool

	// SmpSynch is the smpSynch value sent (0 none, 1 local, 2 global,
	// 5-254 PTP grandmaster). Change it at runtime with
	// [sv.Publisher.SetSmpSynch].
	SmpSynch uint8

	// NominalFrequency is the power system frequency for SmpPerPeriod
	// (default 50 Hz).
	NominalFrequency float64

	// MaxSamplesPerSecond bounds the sample rate an MMS client can
	// select through the SmpRate and SmpMod of an MSVCB, in samples per
	// second at NominalFrequency. Enabling an MSVCB (SvEna TRUE, or
	// [SVEngine.SetEnabled]) whose SmpRate and SmpMod give a higher
	// rate is refused with object-value-invalid. SmpRate and SmpMod
	// writes are not refused on their own, since a client changes them
	// one at a time. The rate configured for the MSVCB in SCL is always
	// allowed. Zero means
	// [DefaultSVMaxSamplesPerSecond]; a negative value removes the
	// bound.
	MaxSamplesPerSecond float64

	// Logger receives SV diagnostics. Nil uses the server logger.
	Logger *slog.Logger

	// Metrics receives publisher counters. Nil disables metrics.
	Metrics sv.Metrics
}
```

SVOptions configures [Server.EnableSV](#func-server-enablesv).

### type Server

```go
type Server struct {

	// controlLife orders control-model value writes (stSeld, the default
	// operate) before Close; controlClosed is set by Close.

	// enginesClosed is set by Close: JournalEngine and SettingGroupEngine
	// return nil from then on.

	// MMS MaxPDUSize bounding one InformationReport

	// ms; ServerOptions.MinIntegrityPeriod, 0 = no minimum

	// hookListeners are the listeners of the hook-routing accept loop,
	// closed by Shutdown (mms.Server only tracks its own listeners).
	// conns are the connection goroutines that loop started and that have
	// not returned; Shutdown waits for them. No goroutine is added once
	// shutdown is set. All three are guarded by lnMu.

	// downCh is closed when shutdown is set; it ends the accept backoff
	// of ListenAndServe. Guarded by lnMu, created on first use.

	// maxConns bounds conns (ServerOptions.MaxConnections, default
	// filled in).

	// Counter of Stats.

	// cb calls application code under a recover and counts the calls
	// that did not return normally (ServerStats.CallbacksRecovered).

	// bg tracks background sends (CommandTermination) stopped by Close.

	// clock stamps protocol values (ServerOptions.Clock); nil is
	// SystemClock. Timers never use it.

}
```

Server is an IEC 61850 MMS server built from an SCL data model.

#### Stability {#hdr-Stability}

The server API is stable as of v1.0.0. It supports variable registration, control operations (direct normal, SBO normal, and SBOw enhanced security with connection-scoped ownership enforcement), runtime report delivery (data-change, quality-change, integrity-period, GI triggers, BRCB replay on re-enable), setting groups (active/edit selection, confirmation, handler callbacks), and journal services (runtime log entry generation with in-memory storage).

#### Known limitations {#hdr-Known_limitations}

  - SCL array/count attributes are parsed but not expanded during server model registration. DA elements with count > 1 are registered as scalar variables.
  - Enum BTypes are mapped to generic integers (INT8) without stronger enum-type semantics.
  - Dataset and report cross-references are validated only within the same logical node. Cross-LN dataset references are not supported.
  - Runtime report engine sends URCBs to the enabling connection and broadcasts BRCBs to all connections. Multi-client URCB arbitration and segmented report generation are not yet implemented.
  - BRCB buffering is in-memory with configurable depth. There is no persistent buffer storage or replay-on-reconnect.
  - Control handlers support SBO ownership enforcement and enhanced-security ctlNum verification, but interlocking, synchrocheck, and command termination are application responsibility via callbacks.

#### Architecture {#hdr-Architecture}

The Server wraps a [mms.Server](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Server) and populates its variable registry from an IEC 61850 data model derived from an SCL file. Data attribute values are stored in a thread-safe \[ValueStore] that backs the MMS read/write callbacks. Call [Server.Close](#func-server-close) for orderly shutdown of runtime engines when the server is no longer needed.

#### func NewServer

```go
func NewServer(model *servermodel.Model, opts ServerOptions) (*Server, error)
```

NewServer creates an IEC 61850 server from the given data model.

The model is typically built via [NewServerModelFromSCL](#func-newservermodelfromscl). After construction, call [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve) or [Server.ListenAndServe](#func-server-listenandserve) to accept client connections.

#### func (Server) CancelTimeActivatedOperate

```go
func (s *Server) CancelTimeActivatedOperate(ldName, doRef string) (bool, error)
```

CancelTimeActivatedOperate ends the time activated operate of the control ldName/doRef that waits for its operTm, as a Cancel of the client that sent it would: the operate is not carried out, OnOperate is not called, no termination is sent, and the control returns to Unselected. It reports whether such an operate was waiting. A control that is not registered is an error wrapping ErrNotFound.

It lets the application end an activation the client that sent it does not cancel, for example before a planned outage.

#### func (Server) Capabilities

```go
func (s *Server) Capabilities() ServiceCapabilities
```

Capabilities returns a snapshot of which IEC 61850 services are currently active on this server. This is useful for diagnostics and for verifying that all expected services have been enabled before starting to accept connections.

#### func (Server) ChangeActiveSettingGroup

```go
func (s *Server) ChangeActiveSettingGroup(ctx context.Context, ld string, sg uint8) error
```

ChangeActiveSettingGroup programmatically changes the active setting group for the given LD. This is for server-side use (e.g., operator override). The handler's OnActiveSGChanged callback is invoked.

#### func (Server) Close

```go
func (s *Server) Close()
```

Close performs an orderly shutdown of the server's runtime engines. It stops pending CommandTermination sends, the report engine (integrity timers, delivery goroutines), the GOOSE engine (publishers) and the journal and setting group engines; [Server.JournalEngine](#func-server-journalengine) and [Server.SettingGroupEngine](#func-server-settinggroupengine) return nil afterwards. Close is idempotent, safe to call multiple times and safe concurrently with requests of open associations and with [Server.SetValue](#func-server-setvalue).

Note: Close does not close the underlying MMS server or any active connections. Use context cancellation to stop [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve) or [Server.ListenAndServe](#func-server-listenandserve).

#### func (Server) EnableGOOSE

```go
func (s *Server) EnableGOOSE(opts GOOSEOptions) (*GOOSEEngine, error)
```

EnableGOOSE creates the GOOSE engine and starts publishing. Call it after [NewServer](#func-newserver); [Server.Close](#func-server-close) stops it.

#### func (Server) EnableJournals

```go
func (s *Server) EnableJournals(opts ...JournalEngineOption) *JournalEngine
```

EnableJournals creates and starts the [JournalEngine](#type-journalengine) for this server. It scans the model for log definitions, registers journals, and makes the provider available as [mms.JournalProvider](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#JournalProvider).

If the MMS server was constructed with a [MemoryJournalProvider](#type-memoryjournalprovider) in \[ServerOptions.MMS.JournalProvider], EnableJournals automatically adopts it so that client MMS ReadJournal requests are served from the same data the engine writes to. If no provider was configured, the engine creates one internally. In that case, the engine records entries for programmatic access via [JournalEngine.Provider](#func-journalengine-provider), but client MMS journal reads will not be served (they require the provider to be set at server construction time).

To ensure full client↔server journal support:

	jp := iec61850.NewMemoryJournalProvider()
	srv, _ := iec61850.NewServer(model, iec61850.ServerOptions{
	    MMS: mms.ServerOptions{JournalProvider: jp},
	})
	engine := srv.EnableJournals(iec61850.WithJournalProvider(jp))

#### func (Server) EnableReports

```go
func (s *Server) EnableReports() *ReportEngine
```

EnableReports creates and starts the [ReportEngine](#type-reportengine) for this server. It scans all RCBs in the model, creates runtime state for each, starts buffering for every BRCB whose DatSet references an existing data set (IEC 61850-7-2 §17.2.2.5 Figure 24 power-up), and begins monitoring for GI/integrity triggers.

Call this after [NewServer](#func-newserver) and before [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve) or [Server.ListenAndServe](#func-server-listenandserve).

#### func (Server) EnableSV

```go
func (s *Server) EnableSV(opts SVOptions) (*SVEngine, error)
```

EnableSV creates the SV engine and starts publishing. Call it after [NewServer](#func-newserver); [Server.Close](#func-server-close) stops it.

#### func (Server) EnableSettingGroups

```go
func (s *Server) EnableSettingGroups(handler SettingGroupHandler)
```

EnableSettingGroups initialises the setting group engine for the server. It scans the server model for SGCB definitions and registers them with the provided handler.

This should be called after [NewServer](#func-newserver) and before accepting connections.

#### func (Server) GOOSEEngine

```go
func (s *Server) GOOSEEngine() *GOOSEEngine
```

GOOSEEngine returns the GOOSE engine, or nil if [Server.EnableGOOSE](#func-server-enablegoose) has not been called.

#### func (Server) HandleIdentify

```go
func (s *Server) HandleIdentify(id ServerIdentity)
```

HandleIdentify registers the MMS Identify handler using the given identity. This is called automatically by [NewServer](#func-newserver) when [ServerOptions.Identity](#func-serveroptions-identity) is set.

#### func (Server) HandleStatus

```go
func (s *Server) HandleStatus()
```

HandleStatus registers a static MMS Status response. The server always reports operational status.

#### func (Server) JournalEngine

```go
func (s *Server) JournalEngine() *JournalEngine
```

JournalEngine returns the journal engine, or nil if journals have not been enabled via [Server.EnableJournals](#func-server-enablejournals).

#### func (Server) ListenAndServe

```go
func (s *Server) ListenAndServe(ctx context.Context, ln mms.TransportListener) error
```

ListenAndServe accepts connections on the given listener and serves each in a new goroutine. This blocks until the context is cancelled or the listener is closed.

Each accepted connection is handled by [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve) in its own goroutine, which ensures that connection lifecycle hooks are invoked. At most [ServerOptions.MaxConnections](#func-serveroptions-maxconnections) are served at once; a connection beyond that is closed at once. A temporary accept error is retried after a pause that starts at 5 ms and doubles up to 1 s.

ListenAndServe returns after the connection goroutines it started have returned (their OnDisconnect included): after ctx ends, which ends their associations; after [Server.Shutdown](#func-server-shutdown), which concludes them; and after an accept error that is not temporary, when it first ends the connections it serves.

#### func (Server) MMS

```go
func (s *Server) MMS() *mms.Server
```

MMS returns the underlying MMS server for advanced configuration (e.g., registering Identify/Status handlers or a FileProvider).

#### func (Server) Model

```go
func (s *Server) Model() *servermodel.Model
```

Model returns the server's data model. The returned pointer is shared with the server internals. The caller must not modify the model after server creation — doing so may corrupt the MMS variable registry and cause undefined runtime behaviour.

#### func (Server) RegisterControl

```go
func (s *Server) RegisterControl(ldName, doRef string, ctlModel CtlModel, handler ControlHandler) error
```

RegisterControl registers a [ControlHandler](#type-controlhandler) for the controllable data object identified by ldName and doRef (e.g. "GGIO1.SPCSO1"). The ctlModel determines the expected control flow.

The registered ctlModel is the model the server enforces: when the data object has a CF ctlModel whose value differs, it is set to ctlModel (a warning is logged), so clients read the model in use (IEC 61850-7-2 20.1), and client writes of that ctlModel are refused with object-access-denied.

The handler callbacks are invoked when a client reads SBO or writes the Oper, SBOw or Cancel subattributes. A control write to a data object without a registration is refused with object-access-denied.

#### func (Server) ReportEngine

```go
func (s *Server) ReportEngine() *ReportEngine
```

ReportEngine returns the report engine, or nil if reports have not been enabled via [Server.EnableReports](#func-server-enablereports).

#### func (Server) SVEngine

```go
func (s *Server) SVEngine() *SVEngine
```

SVEngine returns the SV engine, or nil if [Server.EnableSV](#func-server-enablesv) has not been called.

#### func (Server) Serve

```go
func (s *Server) Serve(ctx context.Context, conn mms.Transport) error
```

Serve handles a single MMS transport connection. This blocks until the connection is closed or the context is cancelled.

If [ServerOptions.OnConnect](#func-serveroptions-onconnect) or [ServerOptions.OnDisconnect](#func-serveroptions-ondisconnect) are configured, OnConnect is called when the transport is accepted (before the MMS association handshake completes), and OnDisconnect is called when the Serve call returns (after the connection is fully closed). This means OnConnect fires even if the association subsequently fails during authentication or handshake.

#### func (Server) SetValue

```go
func (s *Server) SetValue(ctx context.Context, storeKey string, val *mms.Value)
```

SetValue updates a data attribute value in the store and notifies the report and GOOSE engines (if enabled) of the change. The storeKey follows the format "ldName/itemID" (see [servermodel.StoreKey](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/internal/servermodel#StoreKey)).

This is the primary way to inject process values into a running server and have them trigger reports automatically.

#### func (Server) SettingGroupEngine

```go
func (s *Server) SettingGroupEngine() *SettingGroupEngine
```

SettingGroupEngine returns the setting group engine, or nil if setting groups have not been enabled via [Server.EnableSettingGroups](#func-server-enablesettinggroups).

#### func (Server) Shutdown

```go
func (s *Server) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error
```

Shutdown stops the server gracefully: it closes the listeners of [Server.ListenAndServe](#func-server-listenandserve), lets in-flight requests finish, concludes every association (see [mms.Server.Shutdown](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Server.Shutdown)), waits for the connection goroutines of ListenAndServe and then stops the report and GOOSE engines like [Server.Close](#func-server-close). When ctx ends first, the remaining connections are aborted and ctx's error is returned. ListenAndServe then returns [mms.ErrServerClosed](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#ErrServerClosed).

When Shutdown returns nil, every connection goroutine that ListenAndServe started has returned: its [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve) has released what the association held and its OnDisconnect hook has run. When ctx ends while such a goroutine still runs (an OnDisconnect that has not returned), Shutdown stops waiting, stops the engines and returns ctx's error; a later Shutdown waits again. Connections the caller serves with [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve) on goroutines of its own are the caller's to wait for.

Shutdown may be called from OnConnect or OnDisconnect: it does not wait for the connection goroutine it is called on.

#### func (Server) Stats

```go
func (s *Server) Stats() ServerStats
```

Stats returns the counters of the server. It is safe to call from any goroutine.

#### func (Server) ValueStore

```go
func (s *Server) ValueStore() *servermodel.ValueStore
```

ValueStore returns the server's value store for direct value manipulation (e.g., updating data attribute values from process inputs).

When reports are enabled, prefer [Server.SetValue](#func-server-setvalue) which automatically triggers change-detection and report generation.

### type ServerIdentity

```go
type ServerIdentity struct {
	// Vendor is the vendor/manufacturer name (e.g. "OTFabric").
	Vendor string

	// Model is the device model or product name.
	Model string

	// Revision is the firmware or software revision string.
	Revision string
}
```

ServerIdentity describes the IEC 61850 server identity returned by the MMS Identify service. Setting this on [ServerOptions](#type-serveroptions) automatically registers an Identify handler on the MMS server.

### type ServerModelOptions

```go
type ServerModelOptions struct {
	// InstanceDomainNames names each logical device (MMS domain) by its
	// LDevice@inst alone ("InteropLD"), as go-iec61850 did before v1.7.0,
	// instead of its IEC 61850-8-1 name.
	InstanceDomainNames bool

	// MaxExpandedNodes is the number of data objects and data
	// attributes (DO, SDO, DA and BDA, each counted once per place in
	// the model it is expanded to, and each report control block
	// instance) the expansion of the type templates may produce; zero or
	// less means [scl.DefaultMaxExpandedNodes].
	// Beyond it the model is not built and the error wraps
	// [ErrLimitExceeded] and [scl.ErrLimitExceeded].
	MaxExpandedNodes int
}
```

ServerModelOptions control [NewServerModelFromSCLWithOptions](#func-newservermodelfromsclwithoptions).

### type ServerOptions

```go
type ServerOptions struct {
	// Logger, when non-nil, enables structured logging. When
	// [ServerOptions.MMS].Logger is also nil, this logger is passed
	// through to the underlying [mms.Server]. ISO transport logging
	// ([iso.WithLogger]) is independent and is not set from here.
	Logger *slog.Logger

	// Identity, when non-nil, registers the MMS Identify handler so
	// that clients can query vendor/model/revision. Without this,
	// Identify requests are rejected with service-unsupported.
	Identity *ServerIdentity

	// FileProvider, when non-nil, enables MMS file services
	// (FileOpen, FileRead, FileClose, FileDelete, FileDirectory).
	// This is a convenience field; it is equivalent to setting
	// MMS.FileProvider.
	FileProvider mms.FileProvider

	// Authenticate, when non-nil, is called during association
	// establishment to accept or reject peers. This is a convenience
	// field; it is equivalent to setting MMS.Authenticate.
	Authenticate mms.Authenticator

	// OnConnect, when non-nil, is called when a new transport
	// connection is accepted, before the MMS association handshake.
	// This fires even if the association subsequently fails.
	OnConnect func(ConnectionEvent)

	// OnDisconnect, when non-nil, is called when a transport
	// connection's [Server.Serve] call returns (the connection is
	// fully closed regardless of how it ended).
	OnDisconnect func(ConnectionEvent)

	// AllowReadOnlyFCWrites, when true, lets MMS clients write data
	// attributes of the read-only functional constraints: status (ST),
	// measurands (MX), setting-group values (SG), service responses
	// (SR), operate-received (OR) and extended definitions (EX). IEC
	// 61850-7-2 makes them read-only to clients, and by default a write
	// is answered with object-access-denied; the application changes
	// them with [Server.SetValue]. Set it only for a simulator or a test
	// fixture whose peers drive status values over MMS. It is not
	// conformant and lets any associated client change process data.
	AllowReadOnlyFCWrites bool

	// AllowEmptyReportDatSet serves report control blocks that have no data
	// set (SCL datSet absent or empty), which SCL and IEC 61850-7-2 allow:
	// a client writes DatSet before it enables the RCB. By default such a
	// model is refused, because the RCB cannot report as configured.
	// Enabling an RCB while its DatSet is still empty is refused either way.
	AllowEmptyReportDatSet bool

	// NewReportBuffer, when non-nil, returns the buffer of each buffered
	// report control block (ldName is the logical device, rcbItemID the
	// MMS item such as "LLN0$BR$brcb01"); [Server.EnableReports] calls it
	// once per BRCB. A nil result, or a nil NewReportBuffer, uses
	// [NewMemoryReportBuffer] with 1000 entries and no byte limit. URCBs
	// always use the in-memory queue.
	NewReportBuffer func(ldName, rcbItemID string) ReportBuffer

	// Metrics, when non-nil, receives the MMS request and connection
	// events of the server (see [mms.Metrics]). It is a convenience field
	// equivalent to MMS.Metrics, which takes precedence when both are set.
	Metrics mms.Metrics

	// MMS holds the underlying MMS server options. Fields set here
	// take precedence over convenience fields above (FileProvider,
	// Authenticate) when both are set.
	MMS mms.ServerOptions

	// Clock stamps the protocol times the server sets: the `t` the
	// default operate writes (also at the end of a ProcessResponse
	// travel), report TimeStamp and BRCB TimeOfEntry,
	// journal entry times, SGCB LActTm, and GOOSE T and SV RefrTm
	// (with their TimeQuality). Nil is [SystemClock]: the host time,
	// "clock not synchronised". Timers (sboTimeout, operTm, IntgPd,
	// BufTm, ResvTms) run on the monotonic clock and ignore it; see
	// [Clock].
	Clock Clock

	// MaxConnections bounds the connections [Server.ListenAndServe]
	// serves at once, over all its listeners; zero or less means
	// [DefaultMaxConnections]. A connection accepted beyond it is closed
	// at once, before OnConnect and the association, and counted in
	// [ServerStats.ConnectionsRefused]. Connections given to
	// [Server.Serve] by the caller are not counted.
	MaxConnections int

	// MinIntegrityPeriod is the smallest non-zero IntgPd that may be
	// written to a BRCB, URCB or LCB, by an MMS client or through
	// [ReportEngine.HandleRCBWrite] and [JournalEngine.HandleLCBWrite];
	// a smaller non-zero value is refused with object-value-invalid,
	// so a client cannot make the server produce integrity reports or
	// journal entries at an unbounded rate. IntgPd 0 (no integrity
	// period) is always accepted, and periods configured in the model
	// (SCL) are not checked. Zero means [DefaultMinIntegrityPeriod]; a
	// negative value removes the minimum. It is rounded up to whole
	// milliseconds, the unit of IntgPd.
	MinIntegrityPeriod time.Duration
}
```

ServerOptions configures the IEC 61850 server.

The server calls application code under a recover: OnConnect and OnDisconnect, the FileProvider, Authenticate, Metrics and a JournalProvider set in MMS, the [ControlHandler](#type-controlhandler) and [SettingGroupHandler](#type-settinggrouphandler) callbacks, and the code a variable read or write reaches (the report buffers, the Clock). A call that does not return normally is logged with its stack at error level and counted in [ServerStats.CallbacksRecovered](#func-serverstats-callbacksrecovered), and the request is answered with an error: object-access-denied for a variable read or write, a service error for a file or journal service, a rejection of the association for Authenticate and a refusal for a control service. A connection hook or a Metrics call loses that event. The connection, the other associations and the process go on. Code registered directly on [Server.MMS](#func-server-mms) is called by go-mms as it is.

### type ServerStats

```go
type ServerStats struct {
	// Connections is the number of connections [Server.ListenAndServe]
	// serves now.
	Connections int

	// ConnectionsRefused counts the connections closed at once because
	// [ServerOptions.MaxConnections] were served.
	ConnectionsRefused uint64

	// CallbacksRecovered counts the calls of application code (hooks,
	// providers, handlers, metrics) that did not return normally (see
	// [ServerOptions]).
	CallbacksRecovered uint64
}
```

ServerStats counts connections and callbacks of a [Server](#type-server); see [Server.Stats](#func-server-stats).

### type ServiceCapabilities

```go
type ServiceCapabilities struct {
	// Variables is always true (the server always registers variables).
	Variables bool

	// DataSets is true when the model contains dataset definitions.
	// This is a model-level property, not a runtime toggle.
	DataSets bool

	// Reports is true when [Server.EnableReports] has been called
	// (runtime-enabled, not just configured in the model).
	Reports bool

	// Controls is true when at least one control has been registered
	// via [Server.RegisterControl] (runtime-enabled).
	Controls bool

	// SettingGroups is true when [Server.EnableSettingGroups] has been
	// called (runtime-enabled, not just present in the model).
	SettingGroups bool

	// Journals is true when [Server.EnableJournals] has been called
	// (runtime-enabled, not just present in the model).
	Journals bool

	// GOOSE is true when [Server.EnableGOOSE] has been called.
	GOOSE bool

	// SV is true when [Server.EnableSV] has been called.
	SV bool

	// Files is true when a [mms.FileProvider] was configured.
	Files bool

	// Identify is true when server identity was configured.
	Identify bool
}
```

ServiceCapabilities reports which IEC 61850 server-side services are active on this server instance.

There is a distinction between "configured" (the model contains the necessary definitions) and "runtime-enabled" (the application called the Enable method). For reports, setting groups, and journals the boolean reflects runtime enablement, not merely model presence. Use this to verify that all expected services have been enabled before accepting connections.

#### func (ServiceCapabilities) String

```go
func (c ServiceCapabilities) String() string
```

String returns a human-readable summary of enabled services, useful for diagnostics and startup logging.

### type SettingGroupEngine

```go
type SettingGroupEngine struct {

	// key: ldName

	// setLive changes an active (FC=SG) setting with notification of
	// reports, logs and GOOSE; nil stores without notification.

	// cb logs (with the stack) and counts a handler call that did not
	// return normally; nil logs it with logger.

	// connActive reports whether an MMS association is still open; nil
	// treats every owner as connected.

	// clock stamps LActTm (the server's Clock); nil is SystemClock.

}
```

SettingGroupEngine manages server-side setting group control blocks (IEC 61850-7-2 §16, IEC 61850-8-1 §16). It intercepts SGCB writes (ActSG, EditSG, CnfEdit), enforces the setting group lifecycle and the edit reservation, and keeps one value bank per setting group:

  - FC=SG attributes hold the active group's values;
  - SelectActiveSG (ActSG) loads the selected group's bank into them;
  - SelectEditSG (EditSG) copies the group's values into the FC=SE attributes, the edit buffer, which SetEditSGValue writes;
  - ConfirmEditSGValues (CnfEdit) copies the edit buffer into the group's bank, and into the FC=SG attributes when the group is the active one; SelectEditSG 0 discards it.

The banks start with the SCL values per group (Val sGroup, IEC 61850-6) or the attribute's value, and are kept in memory; see [SettingGroupEngine.SetSettingGroupValue](#func-settinggroupengine-setsettinggroupvalue) to restore persisted values. A change of an active setting goes through [Server.SetValue](#func-server-setvalue), so data change reports, logs and GOOSE follow it.

#### func (SettingGroupEngine) GetActiveSettingGroup

```go
func (e *SettingGroupEngine) GetActiveSettingGroup(ldName string) uint8
```

GetActiveSettingGroup returns the currently active setting group for the given LD. Returns 0 if no SGCB is registered.

#### func (SettingGroupEngine) GetEditSettingGroup

```go
func (e *SettingGroupEngine) GetEditSettingGroup(ldName string) uint8
```

GetEditSettingGroup returns the setting group currently under edit for the given LD. Returns 0 if no edit session is active.

#### func (SettingGroupEngine) HandleSGCBWrite

```go
func (e *SettingGroupEngine) HandleSGCBWrite(ctx context.Context, ldName, subfield string, val *mms.Value) error
```

HandleSGCBWrite intercepts writes to SGCB subfields and enforces setting group semantics. It returns nil when the write is accepted, and otherwise an error that carries the MMS DataAccessError of IEC 61850-8-1 8.1.3.4.4.2 / Table 23 (16.2.1, 16.2.2, 16.2.4): object-value-invalid for a group number out of range, type-inconsistent for a value of the wrong type, object-access-denied for a read-only member, temporarily-unavailable while another client holds the edit reservation or when no edit is selected. An error from a [SettingGroupHandler](#type-settinggrouphandler) callback keeps the code it carries (see ErrWriteAccessDenied and the other Err\* write sentinels), and is object-access-denied otherwise.

Supported subfields: ActSG, EditSG, CnfEdit. The client is the MMS association in ctx ([mms.ServerConnFromContext](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#ServerConnFromContext)).

#### func (SettingGroupEngine) SetSettingGroupValue

```go
func (e *SettingGroupEngine) SetSettingGroupValue(ctx context.Context, key string, group uint8, val *mms.Value) error
```

SetSettingGroupValue sets the value of a setting in setting group group (1..NumOfSG), for example to restore values the application persisted (IEC 61850-8-1 §16.1: the groups are non-volatile). key is as for [SettingGroupEngine.SettingGroupValue](#func-settinggroupengine-settinggroupvalue). For the active group the FC=SG attribute changes, with data change reports, logs and GOOSE. An edit buffer already loaded for that group is not changed; the next SelectEditSG loads the new value. It returns ErrTypeMismatch when val does not match the setting's type.

#### func (SettingGroupEngine) SettingGroupValue

```go
func (e *SettingGroupEngine) SettingGroupValue(key string, group uint8) (*mms.Value, error)
```

SettingGroupValue returns the value of a setting in setting group group (1..NumOfSG). key is the store key of the setting's FC=SG or FC=SE attribute (see [Server.SetValue](#func-server-setvalue) and [SettingGroupEngine.SettingKeys](#func-settinggroupengine-settingkeys)). For the active group this is the FC=SG value; an edit not yet confirmed is not included (IEC 61850-7-2 16.2.2.5). It returns ErrNotFound for a key that is not a setting of an LD with an SGCB and ErrInvalidArgument for a group out of range.

#### func (SettingGroupEngine) SettingKeys

```go
func (e *SettingGroupEngine) SettingKeys(ld string) []string
```

SettingKeys returns the settings of the setting groups of ld (every FC=SG and FC=SE leaf of the LD, IEC 61850-7-2 §16.1), one store key per setting: its FC=SG attribute, or FC=SE when the model has no FC=SG one. Nil when ld has no SGCB.

### type SettingGroupHandler

```go
type SettingGroupHandler struct {
	// OnActiveSGChanged is called when a client selects a new active
	// setting group. Return a non-nil error to reject the activation.
	// The newSG is 1-based.
	OnActiveSGChanged func(ctx context.Context, ld string, newSG uint8) error

	// OnEditSGSelected is called when a client selects a group for
	// editing. Return a non-nil error to reject the selection (e.g.,
	// if another edit session is in progress from a different source).
	OnEditSGSelected func(ctx context.Context, ld string, editSG uint8) error

	// OnConfirmEdit is called when a client confirms an edit session,
	// before the engine copies the edit buffer into the group's value
	// bank. A non-volatile store (IEC 61850-8-1 §16.2.4) persists the
	// values here (read them with [SettingGroupEngine.SettingGroupValue]
	// after the call returns, or from the FC=SE attributes now). Return a
	// non-nil error to reject the confirmation.
	OnConfirmEdit func(ctx context.Context, ld string, editSG uint8) error
}
```

SettingGroupHandler provides application callbacks for setting group operations. All callbacks are optional; nil callbacks accept the operation unconditionally.

The callbacks are called on the goroutine that serves the client's request, under a recover like [ControlHandler](#type-controlhandler) callbacks: a callback that ends abnormally is logged and refuses the write with object-access-denied, as if it had returned an error.

### type SettingGroupInfo

```go
type SettingGroupInfo struct {
	// NumOfSGs is the total number of setting groups (1-based).
	NumOfSGs uint8

	// ActSG is the currently active setting group number (1-based).
	ActSG uint8

	// EditSG is the group currently selected for editing (0 = none).
	EditSG uint8

	// CnfEdit is true when the server has confirmed the edit.
	CnfEdit bool

	// LActTm is the time of the last SelectActiveSG (IEC 61850-7-2
	// 16.2.2.7), with its TimeQuality. Zero when the server sent a value
	// that is not a UtcTime.
	LActTm Timestamp

	// ResvTms is the reservation timeout in seconds (0 = no timeout).
	// This field is optional; not all servers expose it.
	ResvTms uint16
}
```

SettingGroupInfo holds the state of a Setting Group Control Block (SGCB) as defined in IEC 61850-7-2 §16.

The SGCB is a special control block under LLN0 at FC=SP that governs multiple setting groups. Each setting group provides a complete set of SE-constrained data attribute values; one group is "active" (read by clients via FC=SG) and one may be under edit (written via FC=SE).

#### MMS mapping {#hdr-MMS_mapping}

The SGCB is mapped to MMS as "LLN0$SP$SGCB" with the following structure members in order:

	[0] NumOfSG    (Unsigned8)  — total number of setting groups
	[1] ActSG      (Unsigned8)  — currently active setting group
	[2] EditSG     (Unsigned8)  — currently selected edit group (0 = none)
	[3] CnfEdit    (BOOLEAN)    — confirm-edit flag
	[4] LActTm     (UTCTime)    — last activation timestamp
	[5] ResvTms    (Unsigned16) — reservation timeout in seconds (optional)

### type StrictnessOptions

```go
type StrictnessOptions struct {
	// RejectUnknownFC, when true, causes browse and tree operations
	// to return an error when an item ID contains a functional
	// constraint that is not in the IEC 61850 standard set. When
	// false (the default), unknown FCs are silently accepted and
	// stored as-is.
	RejectUnknownFC bool

	// VerifyReportCandidates, when true, causes [Client.ListReports]
	// to read and decode each heuristic RCB candidate, excluding
	// items that fail to decode as valid RCB structures. When false
	// (the default), discovery uses the fast naming-heuristic only.
	VerifyReportCandidates bool
}
```

StrictnessOptions controls how strictly the client validates server responses and reference formats. The zero value uses pragmatic defaults suitable for interop with real-world IEC 61850 servers.

### type SubscribeReportOptions

```go
type SubscribeReportOptions struct {
	// QueueSize is the buffer size for the report channel. Defaults
	// to 64 if zero.
	QueueSize int

	// OverflowPolicy controls behavior when the channel is full.
	// Default is [OverflowDropNewest].
	OverflowPolicy OverflowPolicy

	// OnOverflow is called when a report is dropped due to overflow
	// (only used with [OverflowCallback]). Called from the dispatch
	// goroutine — must not block: that goroutine reads the association,
	// so no report is delivered and no confirmed request of the client
	// completes until the callback returns, and a request the callback
	// issues on the client waits for its own context to end.
	//
	// The callback runs without the subscription's lock held. It may
	// call [ReportSubscription.Close] on its subscription: the
	// subscription is closed locally at once (see Close for a
	// subscription with lifecycle options). A callback that ends
	// abnormally is recovered and logged, and delivery goes on.
	OnOverflow func(*ReportIndication)

	// MatchMode selects how the RptID is matched. Default is exact.
	MatchMode RptMatchMode

	// CloneReports, when true, delivers a shallow copy of each
	// [ReportIndication] to this subscription instead of sharing
	// a pointer with other subscriptions. This allows safe mutation
	// of Values, DataReferences, and ReasonCodes slices without
	// affecting other subscribers.
	CloneReports bool

	// AutoEnable, when true, enables the RCB (RptEna=true) as part
	// of subscribing. Requires LD and RCBItemID to be set.
	AutoEnable bool

	// GIOnSubscribe, when true, triggers a General Interrogation
	// after enabling. Requires AutoEnable or that the RCB is
	// already enabled.
	GIOnSubscribe bool

	// ReserveURCB, when true, reserves the URCB before enabling.
	// Only meaningful for unbuffered RCBs.
	ReserveURCB bool

	// LD is the logical device for lifecycle operations
	// (AutoEnable, GIOnSubscribe, ReserveURCB). Required when
	// any lifecycle option is set.
	LD string

	// RCBItemID is the RCB MMS item ID for lifecycle operations.
	// Required when any lifecycle option is set.
	RCBItemID string

	// MaxSegmentBytes is the budget of the segments of one segmented
	// report (IEC 61850-8-1 17.2.2, SubSeqNum and MoreSegmentsFollow)
	// the subscription buffers until the last arrives, in bytes of the
	// decoded segments as estimated by the client; zero or less means
	// [DefaultMaxSegmentBytes]. A partial report that grows beyond it is
	// dropped and counted in [ReportSubscriptionStats.PartialReportsDropped].
	MaxSegmentBytes int

	// SegmentTimeout is the time from the first segment of a segmented
	// report within which its last segment must arrive; zero or less
	// means [DefaultSegmentTimeout]. A partial report still incomplete
	// then is dropped, its segments released, and counted in
	// [ReportSubscriptionStats.PartialReportsDropped].
	SegmentTimeout time.Duration
}
```

SubscribeReportOptions configures a report subscription.

### type SystemClock

```go
type SystemClock struct{}
```

SystemClock is the default [Clock](#type-clock): [time.Now](https://pkg.go.dev/time#Now) with the quality "clock not synchronised" and 10 bits of sub-second accuracy (TimeQuality octet 0x2a, the same as goose.DefaultTimeQuality). The library cannot know whether the host clock is synchronised to an external source, so it does not claim it (IEC 61850-7-2 TimeQuality ClockNotSynchronized; IEC 61850-8-1 Table 32). Applications that know their synchronisation state supply their own Clock, for example with [ClockWithQuality](#func-clockwithquality).

#### func (SystemClock) Now

```go
func (SystemClock) Now() time.Time
```

Now returns [time.Now](https://pkg.go.dev/time#Now).

#### func (SystemClock) Quality

```go
func (SystemClock) Quality() TimeQuality
```

Quality returns ClockNotSynchronized with a TimeAccuracy of 10 bits.

### type TimeQuality

```go
type TimeQuality struct {
	// LeapSecondKnown indicates whether leap second information
	// is known (bit 7 of quality byte).
	LeapSecondKnown bool

	// ClockFailure indicates a clock hardware failure
	// (bit 6 of quality byte).
	ClockFailure bool

	// ClockNotSynchronized indicates the clock is not synchronized
	// to an external time source (bit 5 of quality byte).
	ClockNotSynchronized bool

	// TimeAccuracy is the number of significant bits in the
	// fraction-of-second field (bits 0–4): 0 to 24 bits, 25 to 30 are
	// invalid and 31 ([TimeAccuracyUnspecified]) is unspecified (IEC
	// 61850-8-1 Table 32). Zero means 0 bits of accuracy, not
	// unspecified (the documentation before v1.17.0 said otherwise).
	TimeAccuracy int
}
```

TimeQuality represents the time quality byte of an IEC 61850 timestamp.

#### func (TimeQuality) IsValid

```go
func (tq TimeQuality) IsValid() bool
```

IsValid reports whether TimeAccuracy is a value of IEC 61850-8-1 Table 32: 0 to 24 bits or TimeAccuracyUnspecified; 25 to 30 are invalid.

### type Timestamp

```go
type Timestamp struct {
	// Time is the timestamp value.
	Time time.Time

	// Quality contains time quality flags. Zero-valued when
	// decoded from go-mms (time quality not yet exposed by
	// the MMS layer).
	Quality TimeQuality
}
```

Timestamp represents an IEC 61850 timestamp (UTCTime) with optional time quality information.

The IEC 61850 timestamp is an 8-byte structure:

  - bytes 0–3: seconds since Unix epoch
  - bytes 4–6: fraction of second (24-bit binary fraction)
  - byte 7: time quality

[EncodeTimestamp](#func-encodetimestamp) preserves the full [TimeQuality](#type-timequality) in the UTCTimeQuality byte. [DecodeTimestamp](#func-decodetimestamp) quality fidelity depends on go-mms exposing UTCTimeQuality(); if the MMS layer does not populate the quality byte, decoded quality will be zero-valued.

#### func DecodeTimestamp

```go
func DecodeTimestamp(v *mms.Value) (Timestamp, error)
```

DecodeTimestamp decodes an IEC 61850 timestamp from an MMS UTCTime value. Returns a [DecodeError](#type-decodeerror) if the value is not a UTCTime.

Time quality flags (leap second awareness, clock failure, clock synchronization, sub-second accuracy) are decoded from the go-mms UTCTimeQuality byte.

#### func (Timestamp) IsZero

```go
func (ts Timestamp) IsZero() bool
```

IsZero returns true if the timestamp has a zero time value.

#### func (Timestamp) String

```go
func (ts Timestamp) String() string
```

String returns the timestamp formatted as RFC 3339 with nanosecond precision.

### type TreeOptions

```go
type TreeOptions struct {
	// LDFilter, when non-empty, restricts the tree to a single
	// logical device matching this name.
	LDFilter string

	// MaxDepth limits how deep the tree is built. Zero means
	// unlimited. Depth counts model-hierarchy levels starting at
	// the logical device level (consistent with [Ref.Depth]):
	//   1 = LD nodes only
	//   2 = LD + LN nodes
	//   3 = LD + LN + first DO level
	//   4+ = deeper data attributes
	//
	// Note: the returned root node is a synthetic container that
	// sits outside the depth model. Its children are the LD nodes
	// (depth 1). MaxDepth=1 therefore returns a root whose
	// children are bare LD nodes with no further expansion.
	MaxDepth int

	// IncludeFCs annotates tree nodes with functional constraint
	// information. When true, each leaf/intermediate node will
	// have its FCs field populated with all FCs observed for that
	// node in the MMS item IDs. The single FC field is set when
	// only one FC applies.
	IncludeFCs bool
}
```

TreeOptions configures the tree-building behavior for [Client.TreeWithOptions](#func-client-treewithoptions).

### type Value

```go
type Value struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Value wraps an [mms.Value](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-mms#Value) with IEC 61850 semantic accessors.

Value provides typed accessor methods that return errors instead of ok booleans, and IEC 61850-specific decoders for Quality and Timestamp. Use [Value.MMS](#func-value-mms) to access the underlying MMS value when needed.

Values are created by [NewValue](#func-newvalue), the constructor functions ([BoolValue](#func-boolvalue), [IntValue](#func-intvalue), etc.), or returned from read operations.

Use [UnsafeArrayValue](#func-unsafearrayvalue) for the unchecked fast path when all elements are guaranteed non-nil.
